News.title: Boy, 9, fighting for his life after two-car crash as man and woman arrested
News.content:
CRASH PROBE Boy, 9, fighting for his life after two-car crash as man and woman arrested

A NINE-YEAR-OLD BOY has been left fighting for his life after a serious crash as a man and a woman are arrested.

Police rushed to Shannon Road in Kings Norton, Birmingham, just before 6pm last night after two vehicles crashed.



The boy was found with serious injuries and he was raced to hospital where he remains in a critical condition.

A man and a woman were arrested at the scene on suspicion of causing injury by dangerous driving.



The pair were also taken to hospital for checks following the crash, a spokesperson for West Midlands Police said.

The force asked that anyone with information about the crash contacted it as soon as possible.

In a statement, the force said: “We’re appealing for information following a serious collision in #Birmingham earlier this evening.

“We were called to Masshouse Lane at the junction of Shannon Road in Kings Norton at around 5.55pm to reports of a two-car collision.

“A nine-year-old boy was taken to hospital and remains in a critical condition.

“A man and a woman were arrested at the scene on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. They were taken to hospital to be checked over.



“We are appealing to anyone who was in the area just before and around the time of the collision and in particular anyone who has any dash-cam footage to get in touch.

“Masshouse Lane at the junction of Shannon Road remains closed.

“Information can be given to us by calling 101 or via Live Chat on our website quoting log 4687 of July 28.”

News.title: Frantic search for Brit surfing star, 28, who vanished while paddle boarding off coast of Portugal
News.content:
SURFER HORROR Frantic search for Brit surfing star, 28, who vanished while paddle boarding off coast of Portugal

THE frantic search for a Brit surfing star who vanished while paddle boarding has resumed this morning.

Arran Strong, 28, disappeared in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Portugal on Monday.



Arran was out paddleboarding with a friend near the picture-postcard resort of Arrifana in southern Portugal when he went missing.

The alarm was raised for the surfer around 11.30am yesterday.



A huge search effort was launched to find the young Brit, but it was hampered by dense fog that stopped choppers and rescue boats from roaring into action until the weather had settled.

The search was paused over night but continued this morning as rescuers desperately scoured the seas for Arran.

The star surfer had represented Great Britain at the ISA World Surfing Games.

And he had overcome health problems to fight to compete on the Olympic stage after his 2016 fifth-place finish in the European Under 18s earned him an invitation to represent Team GB at the World Championships in Australia.

Although search and rescue teams haven’t yet given up on finding Arran alive, the friend he was out paddle boarding with posted a heartbreaking tribute to the young Brit.

Jose Maria Pyrrait said Arran was “like a son” to him. He wrote: “Since he was 10 years old, he trained with me and spent weekends and holidays with me.”



He recounted that Arran had come off his board around a mile out to sea, writing: “We stopped off Arrifana to drink some water and take a few photos.

“We stayed there for a few minutes talking, and when we set off again, I let him go ahead.

“As my pace is faster, I always did that. When I caught up with him and gained a short lead, I would stop and wait for him.



“This time was no different, but when I stopped to wait, I saw his board drifting about 100 metres away.

“I paddled to it as fast as I could, dived over and over again looking for him, but we were in a very deep area and visibility was extremely poor.”

He desperately searched for Arran, but he was nowhere to be seen.

Jose claimed “there is virtually no chance that he is still alive” adding: “Strangely enough, he always told me he would die young. Right now, I feel a deep pain.

“The only faint comfort is that he departed at sea, the place he loved most.”



Arran was born in the UK but has been based in Portugal for several years.

He was diagnosed at three months old with a rare genetic disorder and used the clean ocean air as a natural form of respiratory therapy.

Maritime Police chief Hugo Bravo da Guia said: “Both friends were paddling along the coast.

“The wind was fine, the ocean was fine. Nothing in the weather conditions appears to explain a disappearance in such conditions, considering also their experience.”

A well-placed source added: “All the information gathered so far point to the possibility he had a health issue while paddling.”



Portugal’s National Maritime Authority said: “The Maritime Police Psychology Office was activated and is providing support to the victim’s family.

“According to the information gathered so far, the young man disappeared at sea after getting into difficulty while making the crossing from Monte Clerigo Beach to Carrapateira.

“The friend who was accompanying him was rescued by a local fishing vessel that was nearby.”

News.title: Brits to bask in highs of 35C today on hottest day of the week as UK sees fourth heatwave & heat alerts issued
News.content:
THE fourth heatwave of the year is set to peak today with temperatures of up to 35C.

The south east of England is expected to see the hottest temperatures over the coming hours.



A UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) amber heat-health alert remains in place for parts of the country.

It warned the extreme heat could place significant pressure on health and social care services.



The alert, in place until 9am tomorrow for the East Midlands, the East, South East and London, warns that rising temperatures may increase health risks.

On X, the Met Office said: “Wednesday sees the peak of the heat this week, with temperatures likely reaching 35 Celsius in eastern England.

“This would mark the 7th day of 2026 when the UK has recorded 35°C or higher.

“Prior to this year, the record was 5 days of ≥35°C, set in 1976 and 2020.”

Met Office experts, meanwhile, are also warning wildfires could be “exceptionally severe” today as a result of the hot, dry conditions.



It comes as fire and rescue services have responded to 706 wildfires so far in 2026, including 208 incidents.

UK 5 day weather forecast Today: Cloudy across Scotland and Northern Ireland with outbreaks of showery rain, although some brighter spells are also possible. Elsewhere, it will be dry and sunny, with temperatures rising quickly in the southeast, where it will feel very hot and humid. Tonight: Patchy rain will sink south, reaching northern England and Wales, although any rain will mostly fade. Otherwise, it will be dry with clear spells. A warm night in the south. Thursday: A band of thicker cloud will continue to sink south on Thursday, introducing fresher conditions for all. However, outbreaks of rain, locally heavy at times, will affect northern Scotland. Outlook for Friday to Sunday: Friday and the weekend will hold onto a fresher feel. There will be a lot of dry weather with some sunny spells, though one or two showers are also possible.

A National Fire Chiefs Council spokesperson said: “Most wildfires are preventable and we are asking everyone to play their part in helping to protect our communities, wildlife and natural spaces, while easing the pressure on firefighters who have already faced an exceptionally challenging summer.”

They added firefighters have already endured an “exceptionally challenging summer” and urged the public to act responsibly as another spell of intense heat arrives.

Emergency crews have already spent days fighting large wildfires in Wales and Scotland that forced people to evacuate from their homes.

On Saturday, a huge inferno tore through a country park as 70 firefighters fought to battle the blaze in Essex.



And, earlier in the month, three separate wildfires erupted in Manchester and East Sussex as a “major incident” was declared.

To combat conditions, 23million Brits are now under a temporary hosepipe ban in their area, introduced by eight water companies.

The hot spell is then expected to ease from tomorrow as cooler air moves in.

Some isolated showers could also develop later in the week.

Despite the soaring temperatures, weather experts say this heatwave will be shorter than the three widespread hot spells already seen this summer.



July has already been one of the hottest months ever recorded in the UK.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Met Office says the UK’s average temperature so far this month is 17.5C.

That currently makes July 2026 the second hottest month on record, behind only July 2006, which averaged 17.8C.

News.title: Mums told to wean kids on Wotsits & chocolate buttons and a ‘Greggs on every corner’… inside the child obesity hotspot
News.content:
EMERGING from a branch of Greggs with her baby granddaughter in a buggy, Norma Stevens gets straight to the point: “Kids love fast food,” she says.

Here in Gateshead which is a hotspot for childhood obesity, that certainly appears to be the case.



The latest figures show almost a quarter (24%) of the Tyneside town’s 10-11-year-olds are overweight or obese – compared with 22.2% nationally.

Seventy per cent of the town’s adults were in the same category.

Perhaps it isn’t all that surprising when the local health authority shared guidelines to parents advising them to wean kids on chocolate buttons and Wotsits.



In guidance published on their website, the Gateshead Health NHS Foundation Trust published a list of items under a section titled ‘Bite and Dissolve’ for children “struggling to accept lumps in food”.

The list included Wotsits, Skips, Pom Bear crisps, ice cream wafers, Cadbury Buttons and prawn crackers.

It was swiftly withdrawn following a public outcry.

Mum Georgia Dempsey, 32, out with one-year-old daughter Beaux in her buggy, said: “I couldn’t believe it when I heard what they had published, it makes you wonder who’s in charge of public health.

“I have to admit that I have put on a stone or two in baby weight but when it comes to what Beaux eats I am very careful to make sure she gets her veggies and multi vitamin juice.”



Giving nine and a half week-old baby Renee a big squeeze under Greggs’ famous blue and yellow logo, Norma, 63, is not surprised child obesity has become a problem in the area.

She says: “It’s hardly surprising kids put weight on when there’s a Greggs on every corner.

“It’s easy for them to grab a pasty on their way to school for breakfast, especially if their mums and dads have got big families and not much money to go round.

“Unfortunately it’s cheaper to eat convenience foods than it is to make healthy food at home.”

Her daughter Abbie McAdam, Renee’s mum, follows her out of the outlet, with pasties and treats for them to eat over a cup of tea in the cafe at the nearby Tesco Extra.



Abbie, 31, says: “I’m like most mams, I do my best to provide healthy food for my kids.

“I’ll do things like spaghetti bolognese, chicken wraps and salads. But veg is expensive and in places like this in the North East that’s often a really big deal to families.

“You can understand anyone giving their child a sausage roll instead of something made at home when it’s quick, easy and it costs half the price.”

Lisa Moore, 54, walks through the town centre with her mum Enid Porthouse, 76, niece Abbie Porthouse, 20, and grandchildren Freddie, two and a half and Grace, five months.

Lisa said: “No one should ever sit in judgement over parents who are unable to afford to feed their children healthy meals every day.



“You only have to look around you to see the number of cheap alternatives to cooking at home when everything is just so expensive.

“Fast food is cheaper than buying lots of fresh fruit and vegetables and then spending a fortune on gas or electricity to cook them.



“For some people that just isn’t possible and if you’re looking for reasons why those figures exist in Gateshead, that’s your answer.

“I worked in a school where some of the children didn’t know what a traditional Sunday lunch was.

“That’s not because their parents didn’t want them to have one, it’s because the cost of the ingredients is too high for families to consider when the cost of living is as high as it is.

“It comes down to what people have to spend from their weekly budget and sadly in too many cases that isn’t very much.”



Abbie added: “There’s a McDonald’s or a Greggs within easy reach of any of the council estates in Gateshead. They’re cheap and convenient so people will use them.”

Children in the most deprived areas are more than twice as likely to have obesity by the time they leave primary school compared to their peers in affluent areas.

Young dad Charlie Deary is determined his baby son Oliver, aged nine months, won’t become part of Gateshead’s childhood health timebomb.



Charlie, 22, says it falls to parents to instil good habits, as he does with ten-month-old son Oliver.

He said: “Oliver is fed as healthily as possible, he gets his five a day and all the healthy stuff he needs in his baby milk.

“I want him to grow up fit and healthy and as a parent that’s really the best thing you can do for your child when they’re still only a baby.

“It’s down to the parents to make healthy choices for the kids when they’re little so that they grow up with good habits.”

In the town’s Trinity Square, one mum takes the weight off her feet and her shopping bag spills open.



When packets of crisps and biscuits spill out onto the pavement she hastily scoops them back inside her carrier bag.

On the contrary to the overall picture that emerged during our visit, Gateshead Council says one of its policies has been proven to have lowered childhood obesity in the town.

In 2015, the council’s planning team introduced a policy stopping any existing property that wasn’t already fast-food-related being turned into a takeaway.

New research led by Lancaster University has shown the council’s efforts to restrict new fast-food outlets have been associated with fewer overweight children in Gateshead, particularly in areas where higher numbers of takeaways already exist.

The council points out that by comparison to other areas in the North East which did not make a similar policy change, some parts of Gateshead saw a 4.8% drop in childhood obesity.



The Health Determinants Research Collaboration (HDRC) Gateshead team played a key role in the study, making sure the research was relevant to the borough and residents. The team provided a bridge between the council and universities involved to ensure the researchers understood the local context our council officers work in.

Alice Wiseman, Director of Public Health for Gateshead and Newcastle, said: “Creating environments which support access to healthy affordable food is one of the biggest public health missions of our generation.

“The challenge of healthy weight and access to nutritious food is complex, ever-changing, and hard to resolve. There is no silver bullet, and several interventions are needed to create real, impactful, and lasting change.”

Little Evaleigh-Grace Donkin, 16 months, was happily munching on an apple as her mum Alisha Ruddick, 23, pushed her through the town centre in her buggy.



She explained the challenges of being mum to a ‘picky eater’.

“I have one child who eats anything and another who has to be coaxed to eat,” she said.

“Unless people have experienced what it’s like to have to fight to get a child to eat, like my five-year-old, they might not understand how it might be a good thing sometimes to get them to eat Wotsits.

“I let both my children have chocolate and biscuits, there’s nothing wrong with that as long as it’s in moderation.



“You also have to think about how kids are classified as overweight or obese. It is all based on percentiles in what we call the red book, which is the child health record you are given as a new parent.

“Sometimes perfectly healthy children are classed as obese when it’s clear to anyone just from looking at them that they are not.”

Gateshead Health NHS Foundation Trust explained its “Wotsits and buttons” blunder.

A spokesperson said: “We are aware of the concerns raised about information previously published on our website relating to food textures for young children.

“The content came from a patient leaflet developed with clinical input to support children with specific swallowing or feeding difficulties who need help to manage different textures safely.



“It was not intended as general dietary advice. The foods referenced were provided as examples of textures that dissolve easily in the mouth, not recommendations about what children should routinely eat.”

The trust has now removed the ‘Bite and Dissolve’ section, and in its place it says: “This section is currently being reviewed and will be updated soon.

“Parents and carers should always follow advice from their health visitor or clinical team if they have concerns about feeding their child.”

If you’re concerned about your child’s weight make an appointment with your GP.

News.title: Man, 44, ‘stabbed to death’ as family pay tribute and two men charged with murder
News.content:

'LOVED SO MUCH'

'LOVED SO MUCH' Man, 44, ‘stabbed to death’ as family pay tribute and two men charged with murder

A MAN has allegedly been stabbed to death, with his family paying tribute – and two men have been charged with his murder.

Christopher Bradbury, from Stoke-on-Trent, was “loved so much”, the heart-breaking statement said.

Staffordshire cops were called at 7.40pm last Thursday to Ridgway Road in Shelton following reports that a man had been stabbed.

Sadly, the 44-year-old died at the scene.





Paying tribute to him, his family said: “He was loved so much by his mum and partner, brother and sister.

“He will be sadly missed by his father and partner.”

Detective Chief Inspector Ian Fitzgerald, of our major investigations department, said: “Our investigation is continuing and legal proceedings are now active so I would remind people not to speculate about the circumstances of the incident on social media platforms.”

He added: “Our thoughts remain with Christopher’s family and friends and our investigation is continuing.”

Subhan Nadeem, 20, and Dhannish Mahmood, 19, both British Asian and from Shelton, have been charged with murder.

Anyone who has any information or footage can contact us via our online portal here: https://mipp.police.uk/operation/STAFFS26N07-PO1, or Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: American Airlines flights grounded nationwide as company hit by ‘systemwide IT outage’
News.content:
FLIGHT CHAOS American Airlines flights grounded nationwide as company hit by ‘systemwide IT outage’

AMERICAN Airlines grounded all of its flights nationwide after the company was hit by a “systemwide IT outage”, the FAA said.

The carrier was unable to let aircraft on the ground take off and planes had to sit at their gates waiting for the all clear.



The stoppage took effect from 6.30pm ET on Tuesday and applied to all flights and facilities run by the airline.

On social media the airline said: “Our IT team is working as quickly as possible to get our system back up.”



They later continued: “We put a temporary ground stop in place while our teams worked to resolve the issue. We apologize to our customers for the inconvenience.”

At about 7.20pm the airline said “systems are coming back online now and flights are departing again.”

Flightradar24 said American and regional carriers operating on its behalf had 130 fewer flights airborne than the same time last week.

News.title: Moment asylum seeker, 21, is arrested with 7-inch knife and petrol can outside school in bid to ‘set building on fire’
News.content:
THIS is the moment a failed asylum seeker was arrested in possession of a 7-inch knife and petrol can outside a school.

South Sudanese national Both Douk Deng, 21, was arrested after workmen confronted him on the premises of Edgar Wood Academy in Heywood, Greater Manchester, on August 6 last year.



A member of the public earlier raised the alarm after he was observed “behaving oddly” in the street nearby en route to the secondary school holding a petrol can with a hammer tied to his belt.

Deng was “mumbling” as he walked a “full circuit” around the school, which was closed to pupils for the summer, as he scanned the building and then approached it before builders working on site became concerned and called the police.



CCTV footage released by Greater Manchester Police showed Deng kicking over a traffic cone as he walked into the school’s premises and then stamping on another road sign aggressively.

He can also be seen appearing to wave, while carrying the green petrol can, at the workmen who approached him inside the school.

A police car then pulled up near the school and bodycam footage showed Deng wailing as he was wrestled to the ground by a police officer.

Deng is told to “stop there” by the officer, who then tells him to “get on the ground now” as he attempts to run away.



An officer can then be heard saying: “He does have a hammer with him as well. And a hatchet.”

Footage then shows Deng being led away in handcuffs to a police van.

Along with the hammer and hatchet, he was found to be in possession of a seven-inch kitchen knife, and a jerry can containing half a litre of petrol.

A day earlier he was spotted “acting oddly” at another school, Holy Family RC and CE College in Rochdale, also closed to pupils, where he kicked and damaged its intercom.

Deng, who has applied for and been refused asylum on three occasions, wanted to “create a scene for attention” to aid his cause, Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard.



Sara Haque, defending, said: “He maintains that his actions were not motivated by any desire to injury or harm any person.

“This was a bizarre and compulsive act lacking in any type of maturity at a time when he was in deep distress having left Sudan and his family in traumatic circumstances.

“He wanted attention and he was in crisis but he was not motivated by hostility towards children, teachers or the wider public.

“There is no evidence that he threatened any individual.”

Deng, who has a wife and children, was placed in multiple accommodation housing (HMO) on his arrival in the UK, the court was told.



Ms Haque said: “He found himself in a foreign country with very limited English and unable to work because of his immigration status.

“He believed and felt no-one was listening to him and no-one was helping him.

“He felt he had reached the of his ability to cope within the HMO where others in similar circumstances to him had been assisted by the immigration authorities.

“He became increasingly frustrated that the same was not happening for him.

“His only wish is to work and find money to support his family.”



Psychiatric reports on the defendant had not identified any major mental health issues, the court heard.

Deng, of Heywood, pleaded guilty at an earlier hearing to a range of offences including criminal damage and possessing weapons and a knife in a public place and on school premises.

Deng was told he must serve up to half his sentence in custody and the remainder on licence.

Judge Bernadette Baxter told him: “I have no power to order the Home Office to do anything.

“But in my judgment, given your circumstances as a failed asylum seeker who has been in custody for the best part of a year, the Home Office should be doing something rather than nothing to deal with your status in this country.”



Detectives from Rochdale CID worked “thoroughly” to investigate Deng, including examining his mobile phone, but found no evidence of a particular motive or intent, said police.

Chief superintendent Helen Caldbeck, district commander for Rochdale, said: “I’m incredibly proud of the officers’ response to this incident.

“They were professional and brave in tackling a suspicious man armed with weapons and immediately confronted Deng to keep the public safe.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Thankfully no one was close to coming to harm but this was nevertheless a disturbing incident.”

Deng was sentenced to two years in prison.

News.title: Andy Burnham speech live: PM vows to fix social care crisis as he offers rivals urgent talks
News.content:
New Prime Minister Andy Burnham will promise to fix the creaking social care sector as he delivers a major speech this morning. Follow below for all the latest live updates

Andy Burnham will promise to fix the crisis-hit social care sector as he delivers a major speech this morning.

The new Prime Minister will warn the creaking system can no longer be used as a political football while the NHS and families looking after loved ones count the cost.

He has invited Tory chief Kemi Badenoch and Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey to urgent talks today to discuss the problem governments have kicked into the long-grass for decades.

Ahead of his speech, Mr Burnham said: “Politicians might have different views but I’m serious about fixing this issue and to do that, we have to find common ground and listen to others to find a way forward.”

He added: “It’s time to draw a line under people playing politics when the human cost of that means carers struggling, families paying the price and our NHS buckling under the strain.

“This comes down to a choice. We can carry on passing the problem to the next generation, or we can face it head on and work together to build a care system that gives people dignity, security and the support they deserve.”

News.title: New Spain warning as people told 'take extreme precautions'
News.content:
New Spain warning as people told 'take extreme precautions'

A new alert has been issued in Spain

View Image Spanish authorities continue to keep people updated (Image: Marco Bottigelli via Getty Images)

People in Spain have received another urgent warning following a national emergency declaration earlier this week.

‌



Thousands were forced to flee their homes as wildfires tore through sections of the country, although many have since been permitted to return. A new alert from Spain's national weather agency, posted on X on Wednesday morning, cautions that additional fires could break out. The message, initially published in Spanish, reads: "With the new heatwave, today the fire danger will be very high or extreme in most of the country.

‌



"Take extreme precautions." Temperatures are forecast to reach 41C today in the central province of Toledo, where residents from nine of 11 evacuated towns were given the all-clear to return home on Tuesday.

‌



Madrid is bracing for highs of 38C, while Zaragoza is predicted to see the mercury climb to 40C, according to the Met Office. Seville, Malaga, and Palma are expected to experience highs of 37C, 33C, and 33C, respectively.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

The UK government hasn't issued any blanket warnings for Spain, though it is advising holidaymakers to remain alert. The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) continues to urge Brits in wildfire-affected areas to "follow instructions from local authorities and emergency services at all times; check updates from the emergency services; and call 112 if you need emergency help".

On Tuesday, Spain's Interior Minister urged people: "Don't let your guard down" adding that "a spark, a moment of carelessness, or an oversight can change anything". The FCDO guidance states: "Make sure cigarette ends are properly extinguished, do not light barbecues and do not leave empty bottles behind. You can be heavily fined for not following the rules against lighting outdoor barbecues in forest areas.

"Make sure you know the rules if considering a barbecue."

News.title: France wildfires live: Heatwave to peak with 41C blast and winds fanning flames
News.content:
Flames have forced the evacuation of thousands of tourists from the Atlantic Coast to the north-west of Bordeaux with between 500 and 1,000 firefighters deployed in the Gironde region

There are fears horror wildfires ravaging the area around Bordeaux in France could burn out of control again today as a fresh heatwave threatens to peak at a scorching 41C.

The megafire that has burned 42,000 hectares in Gironde since July 22 is "still stabilised", according to the region's prefecture with "several flare ups" dealt with overnight.

But weather conditions in the area are "unfavourable" today, officials said, with rising temperatures of up to 41C inland and 38C along the region's coast. These will be joined by dry winds with gusts that could reach 45 km/h fanning flames by the end of the day.

French authorities yesterday ordered 4,000 people to leave tourist sites along the country’s Atlantic coast, expanding what may be France’s largest peacetime evacuation. The Gironde fire has burned an area four times the size of Paris and forced 220,000 people to leave their homes.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 184 people have been arrested on suspicion of arson since the start of the summer and added that wildfire season is "far from over".

Meanwhile in Spain, authorities have declared a national emergency because of wildfires in parts of Madrid and Ávila and more than 100,000 people have been evacuated.

News.title: Russia on fire as Ukraine launches huge strike hitting country's 'Amazon' and port
News.content:
Russia on fire as Ukraine launches huge strike hitting country's 'Amazon' and port

Ukraine's latest strike on Wildberries - known as Russia's 'Amazon' - was on Ryazan, 115 miles southeast of Moscow with six people injured in the strike

View 4 Images Another logistics hub for Russia’s Amazon - Wildberries - was hit in a drone strike (Image: east2west news)

Another giant logistics centre for Russia’s Amazon - Wildberries - has been destroyed in a massive Ukrainian drone strike.

‌



The attack on Ryazan, 115 miles southeast of Moscow, also ignited a key oil refinery which was already severely damaged from previous attacks.

‌



Ukrainian drones also hit the strategic port of Taganrog on the Sea of Azov in southern Russia, where a woman was killed. Large fires were reported in Kerch close to the Crimean end of the strategic bridge linking the Black Sea peninsula to Russia.

‌



Thick black smoke could be seen pouring from the Wildberries warehouse, the fifth largest in Russia. The roof was seen collapsing and an evacuation was ordered from the distribution hub.

View 4 Images A drone strike on Ryazan, 115 miles southeast of Moscow (Image: east2west news)

Donald Trump urged to help end one war and intensify another as he meets Zelensky and Netenyahu READ MORE :

Ukraine has attacked 11 Wildberries logistics facilities this month, of which seven have been completely or partially destroyed, causing billions of pounds worth of damage. Six people were reported injured in the most recent strike.

‌



Ukraine has claimed that the massive retailer supplies the Russian military. The company is now urgently seeking warehouse facilities in neighbouring Kazakhstan as its business model is under threat with thousands of supplies facing ruin.

Ukraine's strikes came after the US Senate took a first step in overwhelmingly approving draconian sanctions against the Putin regime, with 86 votes in favour.

Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelensky were yesterday pictured smiling together after a meeting in the US. Trump hailed his White House meeting with Zelensky which "went very well" as the Ukrainians sought urgent new air defence protection.

‌



View 4 Images An attack drone from the wave of strikes (Image: east2west news)

Zelensky said both he and Trump wanted an end to the war - but Putin "doesn’t want". He said: "Putin, he gives absolutely opposite messages, he wants a big mobilisation of 500,000 new soldiers from the very beginning of autumn…

"They are crazy, they lose 30,000 soldiers per month … So now initiative not in the hands of Putin.” The Kremlin was forced to scramble to deny it wants up to half a million soldiers in a mass mobilisation this autumn, to be announced after parliamentary elections.

‌



Amid rising Russian opposition to the war, Putin crony Dmitry Medvedev - a former president and prime minister - was sent out to say this was a "lying provocation" by the Kremlin’s enemies.

"This is part of the propaganda campaign ahead of the elections," he said. "Naturally, they are trying to destabilise the situation in our country and create negative sentiment….."

View 4 Images The massive warehouse went up in flames (Image: east2west news)

‌



"I want to stress once again that there is absolutely no need for mobilisation. This is a lie spread by the enemy, which is itself experiencing a shortage of manpower.

"There is simply no one left there to fight. They round up their own citizens like pigs, beat them and throw them into buses. That is what all this is connected with."

But Western and Ukrainian intelligence suggests Putin is seeking a massive new draft to counter the horrific losses he is experiencing on the frontline.

Article continues below

There is also increasingly vocal opposition to the war, and Zelensky claims Putin’s inner circle is split on carrying on or ending the war.

News.title: 'I lost 4st in 6 months by changing how I plate food – I feel stronger than in my 20s'
News.content:
'I lost 4st in 6 months by changing how I plate food – I feel stronger than in my 20s'

EXCLUSIVE: James Shadbolt, 40, spoke about his incredible weight loss journey where he dropped nearly 4st in six months – and it all began with a huge wake-up call

View 4 Images James Shadbolt struggled to keep up with his kids (Image: James Shadbolt)

A dad who once struggled to play football with his kids revealed how a family member's health scare inspired his weight loss journey.

‌



James Shadbolt spoke about his panic when his son woke him up to tell him his step dad Kevin had collapsed on the kitchen floor and suffered a cardiac arrest. The 40-year-old performed CPR on his relative before paramedics arrived moments later. Thankfully his step dad recovered, but the situation was just the beginning for the dad-of-four. The chef described the scare as a blur and "out of the blue" which soon turned into a huge wake-up call for him.

‌



Now speaking exclusively with Mirror, James, from Poole, revealed the health scare inspired his weight loss journey where he dropped just under 4st in 6 months.

‌



View 4 Images The 40-year-old works as a chef so is constantly around food (Image: James Shadbolt)

Discussing Kevin's cardiac arrest which happened in December 2023, James said: "My initial reaction was panic... The whole thing is still a blur. I don't remember having time to think about what was happening or what the outcome might be.

"Thankfully, Kevin made a full recovery, but the experience stayed with me and forced me to think seriously about my own health."

‌



James knew he had to make a change after feeling "awful" towards the end of the year. So when the new year came, he turned to EMDR therapy to help with his trauma.

How a Family Health Emergency Sparked a Father's Transformation

He added: "I realised that neglecting my health didn't just affect me, it could also have a huge impact on my wife [Penney] and children. I made the promise to myself that I would do everything I could to avoid putting my family through something similar.

"My wife started looking at different weight loss options and found MAN v FAT. I'd loved football when I was younger, so it immediately appealed to me."

‌



James began by attending weekly weigh-ins with MAN v FAT, a football league exclusively for overweight men who want to lose weight, before turning to fitness coach Eric Roberts' podcasts to educate him on nutrition and fat loss.

View 4 Images Participating in the football league helped James lose weight (Image: James Shadbolt)

He made a few changes at the start, but nothing too extreme as he still enjoys his favourite foods – like burgers and pizzas – although in moderation.

‌



Next was weighing his portions and tracking his calories to which James added: "It helped me understand how much I was actually eating and where I could make better choices.

"As a chef, I'm surrounded by food every day, so having that awareness was helpful. The biggest change was learning I didn't need to be perfect. I needed to make sensible decisions consistently and find an approach that fitted around my work and family life."

His fitness regime also consisted of MAN v FAT, then once he lost a significant amount of weight – he turned to strength training and joined Eric Roberts' coaching programme.

‌



Losing 4 Stone in 6 Months Without Giving Up Favourite Foods

And in just six months – he already lost over 25kg (nearly 4st).

Now feeling "fitter and stronger than since his early twenties", James said the biggest difference is that exercise is no longer something he wants to avoid.

Not only can he still eat burgers, pizzas and other foods he enjoys, the dad has also seen changes to his resting heart rate, blood pressure and cholesterol.

‌



View 4 Images Now the dad-of-four can run around and play with his kids (Image: James Shadbolt)

Discussing his new "happier and healthier" self, James admitted: "Now I can run around, play football, go on bike rides and be properly involved instead of watching from the side.

"Those might sound like ordinary things, but being able to say yes when my children want to do something active means a huge amount to me. I'm in the best physical shape I've been in since my late teens or early twenties.

‌



"The biggest achievement isn't any particular exercise, though. It's having the freedom and confidence to take part in an active family life without my health holding me back.

"My wife and children have noticed that I have more energy and that I'm much more present. My children also see me thinking carefully about what I eat and sometimes copy those habits."

James shared his story as part of a Benenden Health's new campaign, The Wake-Up Call, which explores why so many men only take action after something significant happens.

Article continues below

The research among 2,000 UK men aged 35-55 found 62% have ignored symptoms or health concerns they were worried about, while 76% admit they prioritise the health of loved ones over their own.

News.title: James Bond and Doctor Who star Tom Chadbon dies as tributes flood in to veteran actor
News.content:
James Bond and Doctor Who star Tom Chadbon dies as tributes flood in to veteran actor

Game of Thrones and Doctor Who star Tom Chadbon has died at the age of 80, with tributes flooding in for the legendary character actor

View 4 Images Tom Chadbon has died (Image: ITV/Shutterstock)

Game of Thrones and Doctor Who star Tom Chadbon has died at the age of 80.

‌



Tributes have flooded in for the character actor, who has had roles in the likes of Doctor Who, Game of Thrones, and James Bond movie Casino Royale. Tom also starred in Peep Show among other movies and TV shows in his lengthy career.

‌



A post from Fantom Events, who he was a client of, announced his sad death. The statement read: "We are sorry to hear the news that Tom Chadbon passed away last weekend.

‌



"Tom was a familiar face to many from his numerous television and film credits, including Doctor Who, James Bond and Game of Thrones. He was always a warm and friendly man to work with and we send our condolences to his family at this sad time."

4 View 4 Images Tom in 1983's Tales Of The Unexpected (Image: ITV/Shutterstock) 4 View 4 Images Tom starred in Game of Thrones

‌



During his lengthy career, Tom appeared in numerous shows. He had guest roles in the likes of Sherlock Holmes, Midsomer Murders, The Bill and Foyle’s War. He also had a regular role in TV show Where the Heart Is.

In Doctor Who, he played various characters, including fan favourite Duggan, in a career which saw him have over 120 screen appearances to his name. One of his last roles was as High Septon Maynard in Game of Thrones.

Tributes have flooded in for Tom, with one writing: "Oh I’m so sorry to hear this. He was a great actor. RIP x." Actress Lisa Bowerman, who starred in Doctor Who alongside him, added: "Oh no… I hadn’t heard. How incredibly sad. He was wonderful."

‌



View 4 Images Tom in Country Matters - The Mill (Image: ITV/Shutterstock)

Tom Baker, who played the Doctor in the hit BBC series, starred opposite Tom, who played Duggan. Speaking about working together in 2009, Tom added: "Oh, and Tom Chadbon was terribly funny. Terribly funny! I used to love the other actors – I was always trying to help them make things funnier, or more dramatic."

Writer Cavan Scott shared: "So sorry to hear the passing of the great Tom Chadbon who I shared many a happy studio session with while producing Blake’s 7, not to mention the storyfilled meals after recordings. An absolute gent. God speed, Tom."

Article continues below

One fan wrote: "So sorry to hear this. He knew exactly what he was doing with the character of Duggan. Wonderful performance. He was part of one of my earliest memories of Dr.Who. Delighted when he popped up in Casino Royale too. Good night, Tom," with another posting: "Oh gosh what a loss, such a talent - condolences to his family and friends."

As well as his role as Duggan, Tom also returned to the show years later to play Merdeen in The Trial of the Time Lord.

News.title: Burnham invites Tories and Lib Dems to social care talks
News.content:
Last week Badenoch wrote to the prime minister saying he should rule out tax rises or increased borrowing to fund social care reform.

A Conservative spokesman said Andrew would attend in Badenoch's place and was ready to work with Labour on measures that improved social care - provided they were not reliant on tax rises and borrowing.

"Social care is vital to protecting the most vulnerable in our society," he said.

"Any changes must be backed by a clear, credible and fully costed plan that delivers better care for the public and value for taxpayers.

"Andy Burnham and Labour cannot rely on vague promises of reform without a clear plan for implementation and detail on what will happen when."

Sir Ed said on X that he would attend the meeting by Zoom as he was with his family in France and had a disabled son who needed "24/7 care".

He believes that the "current system is broken" and wants to see family care "front and centre" of any reforms as it is where "the vast majority of caring takes place".

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "If people are able to look after their loved ones [at home], they don't have to go into hospitals so often and that can save huge amounts of money."

Sir Ed complained about how some individuals face "catastrophic" choices in having to sell their homes to pay for care.

He told the BBC that if proposed changes are found in the Burnham talks on Wednesday that Labour and the Conservatives can agree on, the Lib Dems would support this "even if it is not our preferred option".

He has previously said he was ready to do "whatever I can to find a real and lasting consensus on social care" but pointed out there had already been 22 failed attempts at reforming social care since 1997.

"To see the 23rd effort work, we need to do things differently," he said.

Complaining of the snub, Reform leader Nigel Farage said far from leaving politics aside, Burnham had "chosen to ignore the party that led over 300 national opinion polls and represents thousands of councillors and millions of Britons across the country".

He accused the prime minister of "conspiring behind closed doors with the failed political establishment".

Green leader Zack Polanski, asked on Newsnight whether he should have been invited, said: "That's a case for the prime minister. Actually, I think it's positive he's inviting opposition leaders at all.

"I would like to be there, of course I would, I'd encourage the prime minister to extend that invitationâ¦ The point here, though, is not politicians' personal egos, the point is adult social care is a ticking time bomb."

Adult social care provides state support to help people live more independently, including assistance at home.

Unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use. In England and Northern Ireland, people with savings worth more than Â£23,250 are not entitled to help with care costs from their council.

In Wales and Scotland, different rules apply in terms of eligibility.

News.title: Polanski says guillotine re-post was mistake but refuses to apologise
News.content:
Zack Polanski has refused three times to apologise to Nigel Farage for re-posting a photo of a man wearing a t-shirt with an image of a guillotine and the slogan "we're only making plans for Nigel".

Reform UK's home affairs spokesperson, Zia Yusuf, said the image showed a "photo of man calling for the beheading of Nigel Farage", which he said could be an "incitement to murder".

The Green Party of England and Wales leader was reported to the Met over the photo, which he then deleted, but told the BBC he had not been contacted by police.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, he said he would not apologise for an "inadvertent mistake" that he said Farage had amplified in a "fundamentally dishonest way".

The row kicked off on Monday evening when Polanski shared the photo, which he said was the fifth image in a series of 20 from a party, having accepted a request to collaborate with the Instagram account of a photographer at the event.

Posting a screenshot on X, Reform UK leader Farage said: "If I was to post anything as inciteful then I would expect to be arrested, and so should Polanski."

Asked if he wanted to apologise to Farage, Polanski said: "Well, if I'd done it deliberately I'd be apologising but because this was a mistake I think the important thing is that I point out this was a mistake, that I also make sure that I condemn political violence, and also crucially I make a commitment to be better on social media."

Asked for a second time whether he would apologise, Polanski refused because he said Farage had cropped the image to make it look like he had posted it himself, which he said was "fundamentally dishonest" and only amplified the problem.

Saying he had received a death threat earlier on Tuesday, Polanski added: "The ramping up of the language to say 'this is incitement to murder me' feels like that's also putting me in a dangerous spot."

Given a third chance to apologise, Polanski doubled down and said: "You know as well as I do that as soon as I do that Nigel Farage would run all over social media saying he was correct about incitement to murder and this would all ramp up again.

"I think it's important that I draw a line and don't play his game... It is important that he's kept safe, it is important we condemn political violence, but I also recognise this as the political attack that it is."

"If Nigel Farage wants to apologise for all the times that he's put other people in danger then I will be happy to make an apology," Polanski added.

The Green leader explained he had not read the slogan on the T-shirt when he accepted the collaboration because "what I was seeing was people partying" and he only noticed the man was wearing a rainbow hat as he flicked through.

"It feels quite surreal to be having this conversation," he said, adding: "I think it would be odd for the police to speak to me about that because I think it's quite obvious I've not done anything wrong other than make an inadvertent mistake."

The Metropolitan Police said there was no update on the complaint they had received on Monday.

On Tuesday, Reform asked the monitoring officer from the Greater London Authority, where Polanski is an elected member, to investigate whether he had breached the code of conduct.

Keith Prince, a Reform London Assembly Member, said: "To say that he was unaware of what he was promoting is frankly risible."

A Reform UK source told BBC Newsnight: "It's truly astonishing and quite frankly sickening that Zack Polanski won't apologise for inciting murder.

"He admits it was wrong. He admits it's dangerous, but he still refuses to apologise. Mr Polanski is not fit to lead a national political party."

Asked about the row on Tuesday, Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said there was a "duty on all politicians to be careful about what they post", especially in light of the death of former MP Ann Widdecombe earlier this month.

News.title: The evidence that shows today's 20-somethings really do have it worse
News.content:
Young people in their 20s are facing a tougher start to adulthood than any generation in almost half a century, according to analysis of UK data on housing, employment and wealth, carried out for the BBC.

More than 40% of 25-year-olds are now living with their parents, their wages have stagnated and employment has fallen, show the figures which compare key metrics for different generations at age 25 stretching back to the early 1980s.

The findings are underscored by the experiences of young people themselves who, along with parents, have contacted BBC Your Voice about their circumstances, with many saying they were frustrated about being accused by older generations of not trying hard enough.

We asked the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) to gather and analyse government data, external, for the first time, to see if this generation really does have it worse.

The biggest change it found was where those in their 20s are living.

News.title: Amber heat health alerts to come into force as heatwave reaches 35C peak
News.content:
Amber and yellow heat health alerts are set to come into force on Wednesday as parts of the UK endure the fourth widespread heatwave of the year so far.

Temperatures are forecast to peak at midweek with readings as high as 35C (95F) in the hottest places.

Though the heatwave will come to a quick end for many on Thursday, well above-average temperatures in the mid- to high 20s Celsius will persist into the weekend.

The hot weather, paired with a significant lack of rainfall, will exacerbate conditions in many of the driest areas.

News.title: 'Israeli settlers laid siege to our home': Inside a Palestinian village under weekly attack
News.content:
In Khirbet Abu Falah, right next door to al-Mughayyir, Brahim Hamayel, an olive farmer I met during a previous settler attack a year ago, told me four new outposts had appeared nearby since then - two of them just in the previous month.

He pointed out one of them on a nearby hill - built, he said, on private Palestinian land, in an area that is supposed to be run by the Palestinian Authority.

And the attacks had increased too, he said, sometimes targeting the village itself at night.

"Since we met last year, the attacks have moved from our farms to our homes," he said. "All my neighbours have been hurt one way or the other; some had their houses or cars burned down. We're putting up barbed wire for protection, as if our houses have become prisons."

While we were talking, we saw smoke rising from the village fields. We watched as settlers moved around the smouldering land.

An Israeli army jeep quickly arrived, but it did not stop the settlers starting a second fire, or driving straight past them, back towards one of the new outposts Brahim had pointed out.

This road past their fields, increasingly overlooked by settler outposts, has become a gauntlet for farmers here, to be run at speed in vehicles without stopping or getting out.

It is the only open route between Khirbet Abu Falah and al-Mughayyir. Twice when we drove along it, we saw an Israeli settler sitting in the empty fields.

News.title: Ticket prices set to rise by 15p as Heathrow able to recover runway project money
News.content:
Heathrow Airport will be allowed to charge airlines more for its services to recover money spent on the early stages of its third runway project.

The aviation regulator is permitting the airport to claw back up to Â£320m through higher airport charges to airlines for each passenger. This is likely to end up adding 15p to ticket prices in 2028, rising to 30p in later years.

A bidder which unsuccessfully put forward a rival design involving a shorter runway, Arora Group's Heathrow West, will also be allowed to recover Â£4.1m pounds in costs.

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) and Heathrow said safeguards would be put in place to protect consumers from unjustified costs.

At this stage, the costs being recovered are only for the early planning and design of the runway during 2025 and 2026.

Tim Johnson, the CAA's director of consumers and markets, told the BBC: "We've announced that the first tranche of costs, which is to help with the planning of this, can be recovered from passengers. That's up to a maximum of Â£320m."

Heathrow airport will also be able to collect Heathrow West's costs up to November last year by adding to its airport charges.

The CAA said allowing these costs to be recouped will result in the maximum airport charge per passenger increasing by around 15 pence in 2028, rising to an estimated 30 pence in the following years.

A Heathrow spokesperson said: "This project is about making travel more affordable and giving passengers more choice, while providing a real economic boost to every region and nation of the country."

"We are carefully considering the CAA proposals and will make investment decisions accordingly," the spokesperson added.

In November, the government announced it preferred the Â£33bn scheme put forward by the airport over Arora's alternative plan.

At the time, the Department for Transport said Heathrow's own proposal offered the most deliverable option, and the "greatest likelihood" of getting a decision on planning approval within this parliament.

The CAA's director of consumers and markets, Tim Johnson, said today's decision "strikes a balance between supporting the delivery of benefits to consumers through timely progress on Heathrow expansion, whilst also protecting them from undue increases in costs".

The regulator said "safeguards" designed to monitor cost efficiency would include transparency and cost reporting requirements, and assurance by independent experts.

Airlines often complain that Heathrow is the world's most most expensive hub airport, and have repeatedly voiced concern that the airport's expansion plans will make it pricier.

The government hopes for a planning decision by 2029.

Plans for a third runway stretch back decades, with the government backing the plans in 2003.

However, the idea has also long faced opposition from climate campaigners, many local residents, and several politicians.

They worry an additional runway will increase air pollution, noise pollution, and breach the government's legally binding climate commitments.

News.title: Report on Jewish diaspora finds biggest rise in antisemitism in UK
News.content:
The UK recorded the biggest rise in antisemitic incidents last year of any country with a major Jewish population outside Israel, according to a new report.

Published by the J7 Large Communities' Task Force Against Antisemitism, external, the report also found that 2025 had been the deadliest year for Jews living outside Israel in more than three decades.

The task force is a group of organisations representing the seven largest Jewish diaspora communities.

It found that antisemitism in Argentina, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the UK and the US â which together are home to more than 90% of the world's Jewish population outside Israel â remained at record levels.

Reported antisemitic incidents across the seven countries have risen by 136% since 2022, the year before the Hamas attacks on southern Israel and the start of the war in Gaza, while violent incidents have risen by 97%.

The UK was one of only three countries where reported antisemitic incidents increased in 2025, alongside Argentina and Germany. Incidents recorded in the UK rose by 5% compared with the previous year â the largest increase among the seven countries.

Although reported incidents fell in 2025 in the US, Australia, Canada and France compared with 2024, every country remained significantly above levels before 7 October 2023.

In 2025, 20 people were killed in antisemitic attacks, the highest annual death toll since the bombing of a Jewish community centre in the Argentinian capital Buenos Aires in 1994.

News.title: Brits urged to avoid dangerous plug adaptors this summer - what to watch out for
News.content:
Brits going on holiday abroad this summer have been warned to watch out for dangerous travel adaptors, after an investigation suggested thousands may be for sale online.

Consumer safety group Electrical Safety First (ESF) tested 14 products from AliExpress, Amazon Marketplace, eBay and TikTok Shop - and found they all failed to meet UK safety requirements.

It said in some instances the devices could expose users to risk of serious electric shock or electrocution.

AliExpress, Amazon, eBay and TikTok all said they had removed the products ESF flagged from sale, and that they treated product safety as a top priority.

But Giuseppe Capanna, ESF product safety engineer, urged those "heading abroad this summer to think before they buy".

"What looks like a bargain could come at a much higher cost," he warned.

Capanna also said shoppers should buy travel adaptors from trusted retailers "so they can travel with confidence".

ESF tested six regular travel adaptors and eight universal adaptors it suspected could pose safety concerns.

To be sold in the UK, adaptors must not have accessible live parts and only one set of pins should come out at a time.

But the charity found multiple sets could be exposed simultaneously in six out of eight of the universal adaptors it tested.

None of the eight met the required dimensions and mechanical strength, while some pins snapped off under force during tests.

ESF said anyone who tried to remove a broken pin from a socket would be at risk of electric shock.

News.title: Burnham has no scope to increase borrowing, think tank warns
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will have to raise taxes or cut spending to meet his pledges on defence and the cost of living, a major think tank has said.

Burnham has announced a series of new measures since assuming office last week, including cuts to electricity bills and bringing the bus fare cap in most parts of England back down to Â£2.

But the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Niesr) warned the public finances will continue to be squeezed by more persistent inflation as a result of the Iran war.

It questioned whether Burnham had "fully thought through" how his promises would be paid for, but said the prime minister will have to raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere.

Stephen Millard, Niesr's deputy director for macroeconomics, said: "There's clearly no scope for increasing borrowing, so it is about choices."

Labour's manifesto pledge was to not increase taxes for working people - including income tax, VAT and national insurance contributions - which Burnham has said he will uphold.

Millard said Niesr was advocating for cost-of-living measures to be funded through higher taxes â "which could involve tax reform rather than higher marginal rates" â or spending cuts.

He said: "People have talked a lot about the welfare bill â that is an obvious place to look.

"The triple lock on pensions, that is very, very expensive, and will get more expensive as we age."

He also pointed to potentially reforming council tax to move towards a land value tax system, or scrapping some VAT exemptions.

"Once you've done all of that, then I'm afraid I would break the manifesto promise and would be looking at the income tax rate."

Niesr also said on Wednesday it expects inflation to keep rising until February 2027, peaking at 3.8% before falling back to the Bank of England's 2% target.

The think tank said in its latest economic outlook that it does not believe the central bank will cut interest rates until 2028.

Its Director David Aikman said that "treading water is not enough" to prevent the national debt from rising.

"Every major shock this century has ratcheted the debt ratio higher, and none of that increase has been reversed," he said.

The Treasury said the government will stick to its fiscal rules while investing in "the public services people rely on".

"Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of economic stability and national security," a spokesperson said.

News.title: French Navy carries out 'shooting drill' mid interview
News.content:
A French Navy patrol boat appeared to fire a round of gunshots "without warning" in the English Channel during a BBC interview with the UK shadow home secretary.

Conservative MP Chris Philp was being interviewed about small boat crossings by BBC journalist Michael Keohan as a French warship passed by at 09:15 BST (10:15 CET), about three miles from the French coast.

Keohan said there were 17 shots but "no warnings" from the boat about 300m away, which left Philp believing it was an intimidation tactic to "stop us covering migrant crossings".

The French authorities said it was part of a training exercise, unrelated to the presence of a British ship, which it said was out of range of fire.

Philp dismissed this claim as "not credible", adding: "There were no warnings in place about live firing training exercises.

"It looked and sounded exactly like deliberate intimidation."

News.title: Grieving mum was told baby's ashes were animal remains
News.content:
Ness suffered a miscarriage just before she was due to have her 12-week scan on April 20 2021.

She told how she had treasured the ashes for three years.

"They had sat on my shelf next to my baby scan," said Ness.

In court, prosecutor Chris Paxton KC said "the ashes that Lucy was given could not have been those of her baby".

The barrister did not state that they were of animal origin.

Ness was clear to the BBC, however, that police had told her the ashes were animal remains.

Her disgust at Bush was clear.

She said: "How can somebody with a duty of care do this to my family?"

She and her partner, Callum Ellerby, were told their baby was cremated on 10 May 2021.

"We didn't know the gender," said Ness. "We were not going to know the gender."

The day after the cremation was meant to have taken place, Bush, from Legacy Independent Funeral Directors, rang her and asked her to collect the ashes, which she did.

They were contained in a white china urn with a teddy bear embossed on it, Ness recalled.

When Humberside Police announced they were investigating Legacy in March 2024, Ness rang the helpline set up for anyone concerned.

The force then contacted her to say the ashes she had in her home could not be that of her baby, she said.

Officers explained to Ness that they had checked records at the crematorium and found Bush collected the baby's ashes on 13 May - two days after he had presented Ness and Ellerby with the urn.

She said: "I have felt very up and down. This has definitely impacted on my mental health."

News.title: Some parents on benefits to get up to £4,500 for child starting apprenticeship
News.content:
Some parents on benefits will be given up to Â£4,500 a year to encourage their children to start apprenticeships, the government has said.

Under plans to encourage young people into work, families will be offered a bursary to replace Universal Credit payments lost by starting jobs.

The payment is expected to benefit an estimated few thousand households, who currently face losing between Â£17 and Â£330 a week if their children start apprenticeships.

The Conservatives welcomed Prime Minister Andy Burnham's support for apprenticeships, but criticised his plans to fund the bursaries.

The bursary will be paid for from a Â£30m pot, funded through the growth and skills levy, a tax on employers with annual wage bills over Â£3m.

It followed the publication of a Social Security Advisory Committee report, external which warned of the "perverse effects" of the benefits system on young people's employment choices.

It said, for example, single parents with a disabled child could lose up to Â£340 per week in benefits if their child started an apprenticeship, exceeding the expected apprenticeship salary of Â£258 per week.

Because they are classed as paid employment, benefit payments are reduced to households where young people take on apprenticeships.

The committee said the system was hampering government efforts to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet).

In a recent report, former Health Secretary Alan Milburn warned that one in six young people could be Neet in the next five years unless urgent action is taken.

Official figures show more than a million people aged 16 to 24 are currently Neet.

The government said its new bursary would remove a barrier to young people taking on apprenticeships, allowing them to "earn and learn".

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said: "By providing bursaries to those who need them most and fully funding apprenticeship training, we are making sure cost is not the reason someone misses out."

It is part of a wider package of support for apprenticeships, including funding for apprenticeship training for under-25s and additional support for employers taking on apprentices.

Helen Whately, the Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary, said: "I'm glad Burnham agrees: apprenticeships are a good thing, and we need more of them."

But she said the plan was "uncosted".

"It is spending money already committed elsewhere. So, either it is another unfunded announcement, or Andy Burnham is not being straight with us about his plans."

Burnham has said he is "on a mission" to reduce the number of Neets.

"The trend is rising at the moment, so the first thing I've got to do is to stop that rise," he said.

As he continues a flurry of early policy announcements, Burnham on Tuesday set out plans to strike a balance in the education system between prioritising academic and technical skills.

News.title: Naga Munchetty to leave BBC Breakfast after 17 years
News.content:
Munchetty, 51, is among the best-paid presenters on the BBC's star salaries list, earning about Â£360,000 a year, according to the latest accounts.

She has interviewed major celebrities and politicians on the programme over the years ranging from Hillary Clinton and Michelle Obama to Sir Keir Starmer, Sir David Attenborough and Sir Rod Stewart.

In 2016, she appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.

She has also been at the centre of some controversies during her time on BBC Breakfast.

In 2019, she was initially found to have breached the BBC's guidelines over comments she made about a social media post from Donald Trump about four female politicians of colour.

However, the BBC's director general then reversed that finding after deciding her words were not "sufficient to merit" upholding part of the complaint.

In 2021, Munchetty and co-presenter Charlie Stayt were "spoken to and reminded of their responsibilities" after complaints about their reaction to a government minister's flag. Munchetty apologised for liking "offensive" tweets about the exchange.

In June 2025, the Sun reported details of two alleged incidents which the paper said caused BBC bosses to speak to Munchetty about her conduct.

That came amid reports of behind-the-scenes tensions on the show, and at the same time as the programme's editor Richard Frediani took extended leave following allegations about his behaviour.

Frediani returned to work two weeks later and remains editor of BBC Breakfast.

At the time, the BBC said it did not comment on individual cases but took all complaints about conduct at work extremely seriously. Munchetty and Frediani did not comment on the reports.

The programme won a Bafta TV Award last year for best news coverage for a special about the Post Office scandal.

News.title: Laughter and tears at Dame Penelope Keith funeral
News.content:
Dame Penelope Keith's funeral has been hailed as "wonderful, beautiful and absolutely amazing" by her friends.

The actress, who starred in The Good Life and To The Manor Born, "died peacefully whilst living with cancer at her home" on 29 June at the age of 86.

Crowds lined the streets to say their goodbyes to the "very special lady" as her coffin travelled through her home town of Milford in Surrey before the service at Guildford Cathedral.

Broadcaster, writer and former politician Gyles Brandreth said the funeral was "filled with a mixture of sadness but laughter and gratitude as well because we were celebrating a great actress".

"It was a wonderful way to remember a remarkable person," he told BBC Radio Surrey.

Posting on X later, he said: "There was laughter and tears at Guildford Cathedral this morning - a truly beautiful and deeply moving funeral service for Dame Penelope Keith - what a lady and what a perfect service.

"It caught her completely. She was very special."

News.title: Unsolved Suzy Lamplugh case 'haunts' detectives
News.content:
Police officers investigating the disappearance of estate agent Suzy Lamplugh in west London say they remain "haunted" by the case, four decades after she went missing.

Lamplugh, 25, vanished after leaving her Fulham office to meet a client on the afternoon of 28 July 1986. She never returned and her body has never been found.

As the Metropolitan Police investigation is due to be mothballed next year, cold case detectives say they are troubled by the continuing mystery.

To mark the 40th anniversary of her disappearance, the Lamplugh family has released previously unseen photographs featuring her siblings Lizzie, Tamsin and Richard and her parents Paul and Diana.

In releasing the intimate family images, her siblings described her as "a truly beautiful person inside and out".

News.title: Two-Michelin-star chef brings fine dining to town football club
News.content:
Football fans will have the chance to swap their traditional match day pint and pie for a pop-up dining experience created by a renowned two-Michelin-star chef.

Gareth Ward, the chef behind Ynyshir Restaurant and Rooms near Machynlleth, Powys - which has an almost Â£500 per head tasting menu - has partnered up with Aberystwyth Town Football Club, in Ceredigion.

The collaboration will bring supporters different match day dining experiences, hospitality packages and corporate events throughout the season.

Ward, who has featured as a guest judge on MasterChef: The Professionals, said he was "excited" for the new venture.

The chef-patron said football clubs should be at "the heart of their communities".

The club's team is in the Novira Cymru South division, the second tier of Welsh football.

He added: "I see a real opportunity to bring people together through food and unforgettable matchday experiences and corporate events."

Moviegoers across the world waited in anticipation ahead of the release of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey.

But what about where the movie is set? What do Greeks actually think of the movie?

Conversation about adaptations often revolves around how closely they follow a source text. But in a country where Homer’s story is taught and retold at all schools, many point to how the epic has been kept alive for nearly 3,000 years: not despite reinvention, but because of it.

“What we want children to understand is that every new creation is exactly that — a new creation," Filippos Mantzaris, who teaches “The Odyssey” to seventh graders, said.

The film, starring Matt Damon as King Odysseus and a number of Hollywood stars, follows Homer’s outline: The king's return home from war through gods and monsters to find a palace overrun by rivals.

open image in gallery Robert Pattinson as Antinous ( PA )

In seventh grade, “The Odyssey” is taught in all Greek classrooms.

In Mantzaris’ class, students eagerly debate Odysseus’ encounters with monsters and other adventures. They are taught to compare the hero’s intelligence with his strength, ask whether revenge is moral, whether the battle-hardened king is truly a role model, and whether his killing of his wife’s suitors is justified. Role-playing exercises encourage children to imagine what they would do in Odysseus’ place.

“It’s an amazing literary text, with which children can identify, perhaps see Odysseus in themselves, but also see their own homeland,” Mantzaris said.

open image in gallery Greece The Odyssey ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

Kyriakos Agapiou, 12, said reading the poem in Mantzaris’ class taught him: “That everything is possible and we should never give up.”

Farm scientist Nikos Varelas attended a stage adaptation with his 4-year-old son, after the pair read youth versions of both “The Iliad” and “The Odyssey” together.

“It is our duty as parents, as Greeks,” Varelas said.

Interpreting the story as theater, said actor Manos Pintzis, who portrayed Odysseus in the local production, helps children discover mythology in a way books alone cannot.

“You don’t tell a child, ‘Just read the story because you have to,’ because the child will resist when something is forced on them,” Pintzis said. “When the child sees all of this unfolding before their eyes — that becomes a valuable step toward learning, to willingly learn what they’re expected to study.”

open image in gallery ( PA )

In conservative circles in the U.S., much of the attention has focused on Nolan’s casting choices rather than his adaptation of Homer’s story.

Elon Musk claimed Nolan had desecrated “The Odyssey” after Black actor Lupita Nyong’o was picked as Helen of Troy — despite not having seen the movie. Conservative commentators including Matt Walsh argued the film prioritized identity politics, echoing past fan criticisms of sci-fi and fantasy reboots that cast Black and Latino actors as beloved characters of a different race or ethnicity.

In an interview with The Telegraph, Nolan said backlash “comes with the territory,” adding “these conversations that happen before people see the film — they’re always irrelevant, because no one having them knows what the film actually is yet.”

open image in gallery Cast member Lupita Nyong’o attends the "The Odyssey" world premiere in London, Britain, July 6, 2026. REUTERS/Isabel Infantes ( Reuters )

Nolan told the AP he wanted to make the film accessible and relatable, and “not look back to sort of past Hollywood versions of how to take on the ancient world.”

“You want to question people’s assumptions about how things should be portrayed in movies and what those are based on," he said of his overall approach to the film. "There’s a challenge to that and a risk to that. But my hope is that by creating a cohesive world, people understand the world as they watch the movie and they feel they understand it.”

The controversy hasn't found much purchase in Greece, where people are used to foreigners playing ancient Greeks.

Scotsman Gerard Butler bellowed “This is Sparta!” as King Leonidas in “300.” Oklahoma-born Brad Pitt played Achilles in “Troy.” Ireland’s Colin Farrell starred as Alexander the Great alongside Angelina Jolie as his mother.

open image in gallery A worker installs a hand-painted billboard, painted by artist Virginia Axioti, for Christopher Nolan's upcoming film "The Odyssey," starring Matt Damon as Odysseus, outside Athens' Athinaion cinema, where every film is promoted with a hand-painted billboard ( AP )

Anthony Quinn’s performance in “Zorba the Greek” way back in 1964 remains one of Greece’s most beloved screen portrayals of a Greek character.

Nolan’s version continues the tradition with a star-filled cast including Nyong’o, Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Zendaya and Charlize Theron, with narration from rapper Travis Scott.

In Greece, the small nationalist party Niki objected to the casting and a Greek government decision to provide roughly 6 million euros ($6.9 million) in subsidies to support local production. The party said Greek taxpayers were funding an imposition of “woke-type ideology” on Greek history and cultural identity, citing Musk.

Culture Minister Lina Mendoni offered a blunt rebuttal.

“It is not the state’s role to dictate to a creator how they should artistically interpret a work or a myth,” she told the Greek popular culture magazine, Lifo. “Can we seriously be having a conversation about whether the

open image in gallery Undated film still from The Odyssey. Pictured: The Trojan War ( PA )

Christos Tsagalis, professor of ancient Greek literature at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, said it's ultimately up to moviegoers to judge whether the latest interpretation of “The Odyssey” works. What matters, he said, is whether it captures something fundamental about one of history’s great stories.

Homer’s works — retold and reinterpreted across generations — have endured by becoming universal, he said.

“I think it’s wonderful that something that is created at a specific point in time by a given people is shared by so many people across the globe ... It’s shared culture,” Tsagalis said.

“It’s a fascinating story,” he said. “It is like a movie.”
