Ahead of its release, Christopher Nolan's latest cinematic endeavor, "The Odyssey," was poised to be a monumental achievement, demanding an extraordinary commitment from its entire production team.

To authentically portray Odysseus' arduous journey home, the film's cast and crew undertook an ambitious global expedition, meticulously striving for unparalleled realism.

172: Runtime, in minutes, for “The Odyssey”

It’s shorter than “Oppenheimer” (180 minutes), which was at least partially because IMAX film projectors can’t handle more than three hours. “It’s an epic film, as the subject matter demands,” Nolan told The Associated Press. “But it is shorter.” In case you don't want to do the math, that's 2 hours, 52 minutes.

91: Days of shooting

The shoot happened across six months though it was scheduled for 100 days. The efficient production finished nine days early.

“I found that after 100 days, it’s very diminishing returns. It’s very tough to keep getting new material because everyone’s so exhausted,” Nolan said. “We finished a little early because a lot of things broke our way in terms of weather or getting the conditions we needed or wanted to make particular shots. And at the end of that 91 days, I certainly couldn’t have done another 9 days, so I think the shoot took the length of time that it needed to take.”

Film Review - The Odyssey ( © Universal Studios. All Rights Reserved. )

6: Countries filmed in

“The Odyssey” filmed in Greece, Italy, Morocco, Iceland, Scotland and the United States.

“For me, being on a real location, shooting certain things like when the crew is out setting sail on that boat, or going through a storm, I want it to feel almost like a documentary,” Nolan said. “I want to just put the audience there, like they’re really there.”

3: Number of times both Anne Hathaway and Matt Damon have worked with Nolan

Hathaway appeared in “The Dark Knight Rises,” Damon in “Oppenheimer” and both were in “Interstellar.”

2.1 million: Length of IMAX film shot, in feet

According to the production, that's longer than the distance from Toronto to New York.

“By shooting on IMAX 70mm film, you’re really letting the screen disappear,” Nolan said. “You’re getting a feeling of 3D without the glasses. You’ve got a huge screen and you’re filling the peripheral vision of the audience. You’re immersing them in the world of the film.”

2.5-3: Minutes of continuous shooting on the IMAX film camera before it needs to be reloaded

Instead of being a hindrance, though, it kept everyone hyper-focused.

“That’s an expensive camera. You got two and a half minutes with each roll of film, so you gotta get it in and keep it moving,” said Lupita Nyong’o. “There’s a different vibration on a Chris Nolan set. Everyone is present, everyone is ready, alert, and doing their bit to keep the train on the tracks.”

The camera, plus the noise-reducing muffler they dubbed “the blimp” that encased it, weighs approximately 300 pounds.

5,300: Number of costumes designed and produced

Costume designer Ellen Mirojnick oversaw a team of 175 artisans in Los Angeles and a crew of over 500 around the world who helped bring the costumes to life.

35: Gongs rented by composer Ludwig Göransson

Aulos and the lyre provided the bedrock of the score, but Göransson also used bronze gongs to develop a unique soundscape for the film.

“I really loved the idea of approaching the music from the point of view that’s more the materiality of that world,” Nolan said. “My point to him was I’m trying to do this kind of earthy accessible kind of grounded version of the story … we should probably have the same discipline for the music and just try and create something from a different set of sounds.”

2,000: Extras used to film the siege of Troy

“That was fairly early on in the shoot, and it really brought home to me what we were trying to achieve with this movie,” said actor Himesh Patel. “We were shooting the scene where we all rush in and we’re all just storming the whole city. It’s all going crazy. It is fire light. There’s people screaming. There are people being killed. And the amount of actors and extras is kind of unfathomable. And then Hoyte (van Hoytema), the DP, turned to Matt (Damon) and went, ‘this is a flashback.’…the scale of it suddenly came home to us all that this is just the beginning.”

35: The height, in feet, of the Trojan Horses constructed

That's about the height of a telephone pole. Production has not said exactly how many Trojan Horses there were, but there were more than one.

45: Duration of the 900-foot uphill hike, in minutes, to film the Ithaca scenes

Much of the cast and crew, including Nolan and Emma Thomas, hiked up a rugged hill to Castello di Santa Caterina every day. This is a moderately challenging hike that requires a good level of fitness.

1: Number of times actor John Leguizamo attempted the hike

“I hiked one day. I was like ‘I’m not doing this again,’” Leguizamo said. “I mean, 40 minutes climbing up that 900-foot cliff and then you got to act for 12 hours? No, I took the helicopter.”

115: Length, in feet, of the Draken Harald Hårfagre

About 1/3 the length of a standard soccer field, this full-scale reconstruction of a Viking longship played Odysseus’ ship in the film. The working, wooden ship has 25 pairs of oars.

“All of the actors had to learn how to row,” Damon said. “We went to a rowing camp. We had to really move this hundred-ton ship. That’s not a standard acting job, right? You’re playing a role, but you’re also really serving a real purpose on the ship and moving it around.”

95: Height, in feet, of Nestor’s Cave in Greece, where they filmed the encounter with the Cyclops

The floor to ceiling height is about two letters of the Hollywood sign, stacked atop one another, high. The design of the Cyclops was something that Nolan and production designer Ruth De Jong started on very early in production, inspired partially by Goya’s painting “Saturn Devouring His Son.”

“That was a sort of touchstone for the mood, the sort of horror of it that we wanted to achieve,” Nolan said. “And Ruth came up with a very brilliant idea fairly early on of rotating the eye, having the eye vertical in the face and that just clicked together for me.”

12,109: Lines in the poem

Nolan studied many translations and adaptations to write his screenplay.

4: Oscar-winners in the cast

Hathaway (“Les Misérables”), Charlize Theron (“Monster”) and Nyong’o (“12 Years a Slave”) all won for acting. Damon won for screenplay (“Good Will Hunting”).

32: Locations in the U.S. and Canada showing the film in IMAX 70mm

Nolan’s favorite exhibition format is also the rarest, and some of the most popular locations in New York and Los Angeles are virtually sold out for weeks.

“The sharpness and the clarity and the depth of the image is unparalleled,” Nolan said.

$31.99: Cost to see an 8 p.m. showing in IMAX 70mm at the Regal King of Prussia

According to analytics company EntTelligence, the current average “premium” movie ticket price is $18.22. In 2022, it was $15.85.

$250 million: The reported production budget

But it's not Nolan's most expensive film; “The Dark Knight Rises” is. As far as modern production budgets go, this is in the range of a big blockbuster (the live-action “Moana” had the same), though sometimes they balloon. “Jurassic: World Dominion,” released in 2022, is considered one of the most expensive films ever made with a production budget of $531 million, which accounts for tax rebates and incentives.

$69.95: Cost of the Trojan Horse popcorn bucket at Cinemark theaters

It’s also going for $115 on eBay.

If you haven’t read The Odyssey since high school, Christopher Nolan has you covered.

One of his primary goals was to make his film adaptation of Homer’s epic accessible and relatable to a modern audience.

“It’s something that we all know a little bit about, some of us know a lot about it, some of us know nothing about it,” Nolan said.

“We’re making the film for that whole range of people’s relationship with this foundational text of this incredible story.”

However, the cast list is extensive, and those who don’t know their Athena from their Penelope may feel daunted when heading to the cinema.

Here is a primer on all the characters and who is playing who – no classics degree required.

open image in gallery Jimmy Gonzales as Cepheus, Matt Damon as Odysseus and Himesh Patel as Eurylochus in The Odyssey ( PA )

Matt Damon (Odysseus)

Odysseus is the King of Ithaca and the mastermind behind the Trojan Horse trick that ended the war. His long journey home to reclaim his kingdom and reunite with his wife, Penelope, and son, Telemachus, whom he left as a baby, is central to the poem.

“He’s a very complicated protagonist, which I love, and Chris reveals how and why in his way, and a lot becomes clear by the end of the movie, which explains a lot of how he’s behaving at the beginning,” Damon said.

“I think for a story that’s this big, it’s wonderful to have a character that’s very human at the center. He’s certainly not perfect. And he’s living with the consequences of his actions. And that’s dictating his behavior.”

Anne Hathaway (Penelope)

Penelope, the Queen of Ithica, has been waiting for the return of her husband Odysseus for 20 years.

Meanwhile, more than 100 men (the suitors) have taken up residency in the royal palace, eating the couple’s food and drinking their wine, hoping that she will marry one of them.

“She’s probably the most well- known character that I’ve ever played. But we only know her as far as we can see,” Hathaway said. “I didn’t want to negate anything that anyone had ever felt about Penelope, that she was, you know, the picture of modesty, she’s a paragon of patience, all of those things. But a paragon isn’t a person. And so I thought, OK, so let’s allow that that’s the way the world sees her. Who is she when no one’s looking?”

open image in gallery Mia Goth as Melantho and Anne Hathaway as Penelope ( PA )

Tom Holland (Telemachus)

Odysseus’s only child, Telemachus, has not seen his father since he was a baby. Now grown and with the threat of the suitors intensifying, he goes on his own journey to find more information about his missing father. The two quests provide parallel narratives in the film, which Nolan said is part “homecoming” and part “coming-of-age” story.

“There are times where it feels like you’re on this kind of action-adventure roller coaster, but he doesn’t sacrifice any of the heart and the intimacy between our characters,” Holland said.

Although Telemachus has yet to meet his father as a grown man, Holland added: “Throughout the film, there’s this real sense of connection between the two of us.”

Robert Pattinson (Antinous)

In the poem, there are 108 suitors vying for Penelope’s hand (and the Ithacan throne), including Antinous who in the film is the main antagonist on the homefront. Nolan said Pattinson unleashed “his inner Alan Rickman” to play the part.

“The thing he really focused on was this idea of his relationship to Telemachus. He’s continually saying to Telemachus, ‘I’m going to be your stepdad, I’ll be your daddy.’ It was such a fascinatingly creepy and amusing basis for villainy,” Nolan said. “I just love how Rob based it on real world things, real truths about his character and who he is, and the cowardly nature of that. I think cowardice is one of the hardest things for actors, particularly movie stars, to play.”

open image in gallery Matt Damon as Odysseus and Zendaya as Athena ( PA )

Zendaya (Athena)

The goddess of “craft, warfare and wisdom” and the daughter of Zeus, Athena appears to Odysseus from time to time throughout the story.

“I was like ‘how do I bring to life what is a, you know, a goddess’,” Zendaya said.

“But I think so much of it was in the story and the way he’s telling it. I think the humanity of it and bringing that more human element to this idea of a goddess but what they kind of represent to Odysseus in this story. The lessons that they’re teaching him and why she presents the way she does and in the moments that she does, I think, ultimately, are teaching him a lesson and guiding him through something that’s very difficult.”

open image in gallery Lupita Nyong’o at the film’s premiere in London ( Reuters )

Lupita Nyong’o (Helen and Clytemnestra)

The Oscar winner plays both Helen, the queen of Sparta and owner of the “face that launched a thousand ships”, who is married to Menelaus, and her sister Clytemnestra, who is married to Agamemnon.

“He (Nolan) mentioned his interest in telling this story and really not shying away from the cost of war, actually investigating and exploring it, and so as such with Helen’s character, it’s like she’s known to be the reason for this war. Is that even really true?” Nyong’o said.

“What is her life after the war? I love that we get a glimpse of that, and we really get to see the cost of everything. The rage, resentment, guilt, shame, disappointment, endurance of it all.”

Charlize Theron (Calypso)

A nymph in Greek mythology, Odysseus spends a long period of his journey home with her on the island of Ogygia. Her motivations have been the source of much debate over the years.

John Leguizamo (Eumaeus)

An Ithacan swineherd who is loyal to Odysseus even after many have given up on his return.

“He (Nolan) told me it was the most loyal character in Western literature,” Leguizamo said. “I was like, oh, OK, that’s a lot of responsibility.”

In the film, Eumaeus is nearly blind, which, Leguizamo said, is a nod to Homer, who some historians believe was blind.

Jon Bernthal (Menelaus)

The King of Sparta and husband of Helen, who tells Telemachus what he remembers about Odysseus while they fought together in the Trojan War.

Benny Safdie (Agamemnon)

The King of Mycenae, husband of Clytemnestra, and commander of the Greek army during the Trojan War

open image in gallery Producer Emma Thomas and director Christopher Nolan with members of 'The Odyssey' cast at London premiere: Zendaya, Samantha Morton and Elliot Page ( Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images )

Samantha Morton (Circe)

A powerful sorceress who encounters Odysseus and his men on their journey home.

Himesh Patel (Eurylochus)

Odysseus’s second-in-command who is there for many of the obstacles on their journey to Ithaca, from the cave of the Cyclops to Hades.

“On Tenet, I popped in and, you now, flew, or drove, a plane to a building and then left … Whereas on this, I was there by Matt’s side, you know almost the entire shoot,” Patel said.

“It’s kind of the most physically challenging role I’ve ever played.”

Elliot Page (Sinon)

Sinon, a character in Greek mythology who appears in the Aeneid, is a veteran of the Trojan War.

Bill Irwin (Cyclops)

Poseidon’s son also encounters Odysseus and his men on their journey home. Nolan and production designer Ruth De Jong used Francisco Goya’s painting Saturn Devouring His Son as inspiration for the design, but it was the actor (also behind theInterstellar robots) who helped give the character its soul.

“We didn’t know how we were gonna achieve it. We knew we were going to need every trick in the book, from animatronics to puppetry to computer graphics. But I knew I needed a performer to really look at it and help us find the design of it and find how this character would live and move and so forth,” Nolan said.

“He doesn’t treat the Cyclops as just a monster. And that’s something I’ve very much picked up from the work of my friend Guillermo del Toro over the years. You know, Guillermo is someone whose chief lesson, I think, in his work is a monster is never just a monster.”

Mia Goth (Melantho)

A servant of Queen Penelope.

Corey Hawkins (Polybus)

One of Penelope’s suitors.

Travis Scott

A bard in the court of Ithaca.

Scholars of ancient Greek have been left scratching their heads at Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, conflicted between accuracies and an increase in interest.

The latest adaptation of Homer’s epic poem had an epic debut, grossing $264.1 million in global ticket sales on its opening weekend, including $124.5 million in the U.S. and Canada, Universal Pictures said.

The film, based on the ancient Greek poem by Homer, stars Matt Damon as the Greek hero Odysseus, and follows his perilous journey home after fighting the ⁠Trojan War. It is Nolan's first movie since the 2023 ​blockbuster Oppenheimer, ⁠which won Academy Awards in several categories, including directing and best picture.

For Greek translator Emily Wilson, the release of the blockbuster has been gratifying in various ways. Her acclaimed 2017 edition of Homer's epic has reached the top 5 on Amazon.com, leading a wave of similar books boosted by the movie. Nolan has even cited her translation, notably the opening line “Tell me about a complicated man," as inspiration.

open image in gallery Matt Damon in hit blockbuster 'The Odyssey' ( Universal Pictures )

But the film itself, which has received raves from many critics, left her unsatisfied.

“I want to celebrate the fact that so many more people are aware of The Odyssey and were brought back to the poem,” she told The Associated Press. ”But at the same time, I had the sense that Christopher Nolan was trying to pack everything in while missing themes that were essential to the poem."

Reviewers have praised the acting and the narrative drive, the grand scale of a movie shot entirely on IMAX film and how it weds the sensibilities of ancient Greece and the modern world, at least as Nolan perceives it.

open image in gallery Stars of The Odyssey with director Christopher Nolan ( AP )

The divide between scholars and critics seems in part a matter of whether the balance should tilt toward Nolan or Homer. Wilson and fellow translator Daniel Mendelsohn both expressed admiration for Nolan's cinematic flair and ambition, what Mendelsohn calls his “great visual panache.” Both speculated that his desire to make a “Christopher Nolan” movie led to unfortunate decisions.

Mendelsohn is an author, critic and translator and his assessment appeared Friday in The New York Review of Books, where he is an editor-at-large.

Mendelsohn had previously defended Nolan's controversial decision to cast a Black actor, Lupita Nyong’o, as Helen of Troy, calling it a worthy way to “provoke, challenge and discomfit how we think about beauty and identity.” But he faulted the director for giving us an Odysseus with “no cleverness, no humor, no wily charm.” One of the Western canon's formative tricksters has been transformed, he contended, into the kind of haunted protagonist featured in such previous Nolan movies as Oppenheimer and Memento.

"This tormented, guilt-ridden Odysseus, stripped of humor and wit, seductiveness and cleverness, is a sibling of Memento’s anguished amnesiac, of Batman, of Oppenheimer, men tormented by pasts they wrestle with in different ways," wrote Mendelsohn, whose Odyssey translation came out in 2025. “Nolan has merely remade Homer’s hero in his own image.”

open image in gallery Matt Damon as Odysseus, left, and Zendaya as Athena, in a scene from ‘The Odyssey’ ( © Universal Studios. All Rights Reserved. )

Wilson, a professor of classical studies at the University of Pennsylvania, said she didn't want to come across as a “snobby,” nitpicking expert at odds with any deviation from the original text. But she questioned a range of omissions and other choices, from the absence on screen of the Gods Zeus and Poseidon (Athena is played by Zendaya ) to the “incoherent” messaging that condemns both war and physical cowardice. She found Penelope's role so thinned out that it endangered “any possibility of believing in this marriage.” Wilson also that thought parts of the movie, notably the scenes with Odysseus' dog, Argos, “catered towards modern sentimentality.”

“Everybody's a sucker for a dog,” she said.

open image in gallery ( PA )

A spokesperson for Nolan did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Wilson declined to offer a grade or ranking for the movie, but said she would recommend it for others, as long as they see it in a cinema.

“It was fun to be there with my kids. I didn’t feel it was pulling teeth to engage with it,” she said. “If you can see it on a big screen you should absolutely go."

A man who fears persecution in Iran has spent 15 years in the UK battling a failed asylum claim, homeless and unable to lead a normal life, after repeated refusals by the Home Office to allow him to stay.

In the more than a decade he has been trapped in the asylum system, Mostafa Rahmani has not been allowed to work or been housed in Home Office accommodation – forced to depend on the kindness of friends to get by.

Mr Rahmani, now 41, he arrived in the UK from Iran in 2011 as a 26-year-old student looking to learn English. He came on a student visa, but claimed asylum a few days after arrival when he says Iranian security forces turned up at his family’s home in Tehran looking for him. He said that he had taken part in anti-government protests in 2011.

Since 2012, he has been involved in an Iranian women’s rights campaign group in the UK, called 8mars, relying on its members for support and friendship. He says he is at risk of persecution and death at the hands of Iran’s security forces if he returns due to his anti-government campaigning. But the Home Office disagrees, saying that Mr Rahmani does not hold a sufficient political profile in the UK or Iran to be considered at such risk.

Mr Rahmani, supported by Birchtree Law Chambers law firm, has had his asylum application rejected several times and is now waiting to hear the Home Office’s verdict of his latest challenge.

open image in gallery Mostafa pictured in Iran before he came to the UK on a student visa ( Mostafa Rahmani )

Speaking about his time in limbo in the UK, Mr Rahmani told The Independent: “My programme and dreams for my life, for years and years, are all gone.”

He explained: “I used to sleep in the street, and in an Asda parking area, or on buses. Often big apartment blocks have rubbish rooms, and when it was cold I would sleep there. One supermarket was in Wembley, another was in Acton. Sometimes I would stay in churches and they would give me food.

“I made friends and I could go to different places to shower if I needed, around Enfield and Acton.”

open image in gallery Mostafa Rahmani has been a supporter of an Iranian womens’ rights group since 2012 ( Mostafa Rahmani )

“It is only recently that I have been allowed accommodation from the Home Office, but even now it is sometimes better to live on the road than stay in their accommodation. I have to share a bunk bed with a man who talks all the time to his family back in Afghanistan, which makes it hard to sleep. So when that happens, I go out and look for a bus to sleep.”

Iran has been the most common country of nationality among asylum applicants and small boat arrivals to the UK in recent years. Around 63,000 Iranian citizens applied for asylum in the UK in the decade between 2016 and 2025, according to data analysis by the University of Oxford’s Migration Observatory.

Last year, 58 per cent of Iranians were granted asylum the first time they applied. However, those who are refused are unlikely to be sent back as very few Iranians are deported due to the country’s terrible human rights record, and since March 2026, conflict with the US and Israel has engulfed the country and wider Middle East region. In the first three months of 2026, 42 Iranians were forcibly deported from the UK, and 15 people returned voluntarily, Home Office data shows.

Mr Rahmani described his life before the UK, saying: “Back in Iran I had my own car, I had my father to support me, I had a good life, I had my own room. My situation here, it is not comparable to the standard of living that I had. I thought about going back to Iran so many times, but the Iranian government kill and hang people and I know I cannot.

“Most of all I wish for a visa so that I can go abroad to see my mum, who is 70 years old. I hope that I can one day meet my parents in Turkey, before anything happens to them. My friend got his visa after eight years but his mother died before they could reunite – I am worried this will happen to me.”

open image in gallery Mostafa Rahmani, an Iranian asylum seeker who has been in immigration limbo for 15 years ( The Independent )

His friend Leila Parnian, a member of 8mars has known him for 20 years. Speaking about his time in the UK, she explained: “They did not give him a chance to live like a normal person. He doesn’t have a future, a life, kids or work. He’s stuck here. For 15-16 years, they have played with his life and he doesn’t have anything. Not even one room for himself to do what he wants.

“He doesn’t know what to do with his life, he cannot stay here like this. He cannot go back to his country. Every day the Islamic regime is hanging young people. It’s not fair, to play with somebody’s life for nearly 16 years, without any reason.

“He came as a young person and he is now 41, and he has nothing in his hands.”

Rashad Nawaz, director at Birchtree Law which is supporting his asylum application, said: “Having worked on Mr Rahmani’s case I can say he is genuinely committed to his cause and has over a decade consistently informed the secretary of state about his work campaigning for women’s rights in Iran.

“8mars have very clearly stated that his life would be in danger upon return to Iran because of his political activities in the UK. Mr Rahmani puts on a brave face when facing the world but I have witnessed first-hand his mental health deteriorating.

“It is frankly bizarre for the secretary of state to consistently deny Mr Rahmani permission to stay when she cannot remove him to Iran because she accepts Iran has an awful human rights record. I hope sense will prevail and he is given permission to stay."

The Home Office said it does not comment on individual cases.

Electric vehicle charging stations in an affluent Delhi neighbourhood, bustling with scooters, trucks, and cars near a popular shopping area, highlight the city's urgent need for expanded infrastructure.

Despite ambitious plans to phase out petrol vehicles in one of the world’s most polluted cities, drivers report a significant shortfall in charging facilities.

Shyam Singh, a marketing executive who owns a two-wheel electric scooter, highlighted the issue, stating: "Charging facilities are not up to the mark yet."

He added that the current battery range makes it hard for long-distance drivers to switch to EVs.

Delhi uses a bold approach to mainstream EVs

Delhi adopted a new policy on 1 July that aims to make the vast majority of newly registered vehicles electric by 2027. While existing gas-powered vehicles won't be banned, their numbers are expected to dwindle in the coming years.

Energy experts say the plan is one of the country’s most ambitious electric-vehicle policies and a significant step toward improving the city's air quality and reducing pollution.

open image in gallery Delhi adopted a new policy on 1 July that aims to make the vast majority of newly registered vehicles electric by 2027 ( Associated Press )

The policy provides EV buyers with subsidies and waivers on registration fees and some road taxes, incentives to scrap gas vehicles, and it offers plans to expand the charging infrastructure.

It also targets two- and three-wheelers that make up nearly 70 per cent of vehicles in the city: Starting in 2027, any newly registered three-wheeled vehicles and small trucks must be electric, with two-wheelers the following year.

Currently, only about 5 per cent of the 8.7 million vehicles registered in Delhi are electric. But EV registrations have been increasing, with over 100,000 in the past year, most of them two- and three-wheelers. Registrations for new gas-powered cars and bigger trucks will still be allowed for the time being.

The plan, which is expected to cost the local government 150 billion rupees ($1.5 billion), will offer cash amounts of up to 50,000 rupees ($522) for residents who purchase EVs and up to 100,000 rupees ($1,044) for those who scrap their old gasoline-powered vehicles.

“Delhi’s EV policy is one of the most ambitious policies that I have seen in India,” said Jaideep Saraswat, who leads work on clean power and electric mobility at the Vasudha Foundation.

The deadlines, he added, send a signal to automakers and consumers that change is “inevitable.”

While states including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have offered incentives for electric vehicle owners and manufacturers, cut taxes and pumped money into setting up charging stations, Delhi is the first to phase out gas-powered vehicles.

open image in gallery Currently, only about 5 per cent of the 8.7 million vehicles registered in Delhi are electric ( Associated Press )

Going electric can reduce pollution

Severe air pollution in Delhi frequently forces school closures, construction bans and emergency public health measures, especially during the winter months. Vehicles cause about a quarter of air pollution in the National Capital Region surrounding Delhi, and two- and three-wheelers are responsible for nearly half of vehicular pollution in the city.

Ruchita Shah, an energy analyst for the global energy think tank Ember, said the city has long been a clean energy pioneer, including its earlier shift toward compressed natural gas vehicles to cut pollution.

She said electric vehicles accounted for about 12.7 per cent of Delhi’s new vehicle sales in the 2026 financial year, compared with 8.3 per cent nationally.

The new policy’s most forward-looking feature, she said, is linking subsidies to tight deadlines after which some internal combustion engine vehicles can no longer be newly registered.

Sunil Dahiya, founder of environmental research organization Envirocatalyst, said cleaner vehicles could significantly reduce public exposure to roadside emissions. Still, he cautioned that the benefits will take time to fully materialize because existing gasoline, diesel, and CNG vehicles will continue to operate for years.

Charging infrastructure is a key hurdle

Some owners of gasoline-powered two-wheelers say this isn't the right time to go electric.

Siddhant Jha, a 22-year-old software engineer and northern Delhi resident, is worried about the longevity of EVs compared with his traditional two-wheeler, and the annual street flooding damaging a vehicle’s electrical components.

“I'd like to wait for a few years for better models and the 150,000 rupees ($1,566) I'll spend (on an EV) will make more sense then.”

Jha is also concerned about EV charging accessibility.

open image in gallery Vehicles cause about a quarter of air pollution in the National Capital Region surrounding Delhi, and two- and three-wheelers are responsible for nearly half of vehicular pollution in the city. ( Associated Press )

Shah, the energy analyst, said the policy’s success hinges on Delhi building sufficient charging infrastructure and sourcing more supplied power from renewable resources rather than fossil fuel plants. Most vehicle charging now happens at night, when solar power is unavailable, forcing the dependence on thermal power plants to meet demand.

Delhi must also upgrade its electricity grid — especially fast chargers needed by buses, cargo vehicles and cars — to meet the surge in demand and avoid grid failures, said Dahiya, the environmentalist.

Dahiya recommended installing battery storage at charging stations and adopting time-of-day pricing to incentivize charging when renewable power is more abundant.

Delhi's next challenges will be coordinating with surrounding states to decarbonize the electricity grid and public transport electrification, said Saraswat of the Vasudha Foundation.

“As a resident of Delhi, I’m sure each and every one will be extremely thrilled to have this policy. To see that winter where there is no smog, no pollution.”

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at the 2018 Commonwealth Games in Australia and was selected again for this summer’s Games in Glasgow.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham’s model girlfriend Ashlyn shows off her beach body in bikini on sun-soaked holiday after World Cup
Sports.content:
JUDE BELLINGHAM’s Wag Ashlyn Castro has shown off her stunning body on holiday.

The black- haired model posed for some snaps on the beach in a light bikini.



Sat on a towel in the sun, Ashlyn, 28, had her eyes closed and hands on her bottom with sandy legs tucked underneath her body.

With her dark hair plaited and tied up, the busty girlfriend dazzled on vacation.



She has spent much of the summer travelling around the USA to watch Bellingham with England.

Ashlyn was regularly seen with other Wags and Bellingham‘s family at games.

She chilled with dad Mark and consoled her Real Madrid partner following the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Huge social media hit Ashlyn has over 1million Insta followers.



But she rarely posts pics of Jude online, instead sticking to her glam life and fancy outfits.

The pair have been together since 2024 and Ashlyn used to date The Wire actor Michael B Jordan, who is now an investor at Bournemouth and an Oscar winner for his joint role in Sinners.



Ashlyn has also been seen hanging out with Bellingham’s mum Denise in the stands.

She regularly uploads snaps of herself in revealing dresses and glitzy fits.

Bellingham has been described by her as “the most thoughtful, kind-hearted, hard-working, incredible human I’ve ever known.”

They were spotted smooching after a game at the World Cup with Ashlyn attending alongside Megan Pickford and others.



Their love life is mostly private however.

The midfielder, 31, became a free agent when he walked away from Sheffield Wednesday at the end of last season.



And Charlton boss Nathan Jones has decided to give Chalobah an opportunity to reignite his career in the second tier.

He came off the bench during the Addicks’ pre-season win over Colchester United last night.



Chalobah replaced Charlton fan favourite Conor Coventry just after the hour mark to give Jones the chance to run the rule over him.

The South Londoners, who will face Reading in their final warm-up showdown on Saturday, are tempted to land the former Chelsea youngster as a free agent if he impresses during his trial.

Chalobah made 13 appearances for Sheffield Wednesday last season, notching two goals and one assist along the way.

But he could not stop the crisis club making unwanted history as they were relegated to League One in FEBRUARY.

Sheffield Wednesday were deducted 18 points for financial mismanagement and staff went unpaid for several months during a chaotic campaign.

Chalobah paid an emotional tribute to the Hillsborough faithful when his exit was confirmed.

Sports.title: Why ‘dictator’ Gianni Infantino’s shameful plot to sell World Cup is destined to succeed despite Uefa’s furious backlash
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO sent shockwaves through football with his latest plan to change the game as we know it.

Fifa announced on Tuesday that they are looking into setting up a company which would essentially sell stakes in the World Cup.



The outcry from those in football has been great, with Uefa leading the way via a scathing statement.

The governing body said the outlandish scheme “crosses a line” and is said to be holding an emergency summit with its members shortly.



The statement concluded: “The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially.

“None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”



Uefa’s feelings are shared by the majority if not all fans – but it is not impossible to imagine these radical new plans being waved through.

No one would have predicted a winter World Cup in Qatar such was the initial outrage, yet that was exactly what we got four years ago.

Infantino’s power is clear for all to see and other leading names in football are wary of the stranglehold he seemingly has.

La Liga president, Javier Tebas, recently told Italian newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport: “He has the support of the system, of the federations.



“There is no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. It is a system rotten at its core.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Former Fifa president Sepp Blatter, in an interview with Politico earlier this year, described Fifa as a “dictatorship”.

There has been uproar in parts over a number of actions, such as the expanded Club World Cup last year and the fiasco around Folarin Balogun’s suspension reprieve at the World Cup.

This latest proposal has been met with backlash, too, and there have been reports European nations could boycott the World Cup.



Opposing the plans, UK PM Burnham wrote on X: “Let me say this very directly.

“Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

“The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.

“Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.”

Ex-Liverpool player Stan Collymore suggested Uefa should split from Fifa, adding: “Uefa’s power base is 10, 20, 1,000 times more. It’s where all the players, storied clubs, monster crowds, greatest coaches, referees and sheer size of football infrastructure is.”



Gary Lineker reposted the BBC’s Instagram story with the comment “Nothing surprises me any more” and a vomit emoji.

Infantino, for his part, can point to the huge revenues Fifa have generated since his time at the helm over the past ten years to explain his popularity.

And if this latest scheme is to get the green light, it will require the majority support of Fifa’s 211 member associations and the governing body’s Council.

There are a few reasons – well, actually, a million or so reasons – why they could be on board with them.

Fifa are proposing to create a company – the Fifa Forward Enterprise – that would bring together their commercial rights and tournament delivery.



Investors would be able to purchase “minority, non-controlling interests”, but Fifa would crucially retain exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendars and all regulatory and sporting decisions.

The governing body explained in its statement on Tuesday how all of its 211 member associations would benefit from Fifa’s “football development funding” increasing to over £7.5billion over the next four years.

That would manifest itself in the shape of the FIFA Fast Forward Programme, which would allow member associations to unlock additional development funding.



All 211 member associations would be invited to participate in the programme, which would give them access to a one-off lump sum each of $20million (£15m).

This could be used for projects such as stadiums and national training centres, and other long-term infrastructure.

The funding for that would be financed via Fifa’s new company, Fifa Forward Enterprise, and the capital raised from it.

Fifa estimates this figure will be $4.2billion (£3.2billion) due to the company being valued at $20bn (£15bn).

As well as possible access to a one-off lump sum, Fifa are forecasting member associations’ funding to increase.



The upcoming cycle from 2027-30 was budgeted at $8m (£6m) per member association, but Fifa say that would rise to $20m (£15m).

It would continue to increase for the next two cycles and the 2035-38 one would see each member association receive $24m (£18m) via Fifa Forward – the governing body’s flagship development programme.

Fifa has explained how that money could then be used to support infrastructure, coaching, national teams, competitions, grassroots football and the women’s game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Infantino said: “Every Fifa member association, whatever its size, resources, or geographic location will have a voice and the opportunity to determine its own course.

“Football has become a truly global game and so the benefits must be felt globally.”

Sports.title: EFL club’s former stadium set to be largely demolished with historic stands knocked down in fresh plans
Sports.content:
ROTHERHAM UNITED’S former Millmoor home will be largely demolished if plans submitted to local councillors are approved.

The project, if given the green light, is set to see two of the ground’s stands torn down, in addition to some surrounding buildings.



The Millers left Millmoor in 2008 after new owner Tony Stewart failed to agree a deal with former chief Ken Booth.

Booth had saved the club from financial turmoil in 1987 but decided to depart in 2004 amid rising debts following the ITV Digital collapse that crippled much of the EFL.



The Booth family gave the club away to a supporter group for £1, while also writing off its overdraft.

But in the deal they insisted on keeping several assets; the club’s Hooton Lodge training ground, land on which stood the Tivoli nightclub and even priority ticket access among them.



Most significantly, the deal saw the Booth family retain ownership of Millmoor.

A turbulent few years followed, as the club edged closer to oblivion.



When Stewart rescued Rotherham after they’d been plunged into ruin once again, he was unable to secure Millmoor as part of his deal to acquire the Yorkshire club from the Booth family, despite his best efforts.

As a result, the Millers spent four years at the Don Valley athletics stadium in Sheffield before moving into the swanky modern New York Stadium a stone’s throw from Millmoor.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

At the time of Rotherham’s exit they had been halfway through a rebuild of the club’s main stand… a rebuild that would never finish.

For more than a decade after the Millers’ exit, Millmoor was left largely to rot.



Rotherham Titans, a second-tier rugby club, had shared the ground with United on occasion during the early 2000s.

In 2011 they attempted to strike a deal to use Millmoor, three years on from the football club’s departure.

But like Stewart, they could not strike a deal with the Booth family.

The ground began to fall into a state of disrepair, with its stands growing ever more dilapidated.



Remarkably, much of Millmoor did actually stay relatively intact down the years, with its pitch somewhat maintained, its goals still standing and most of its signage remaining.

In a further twist, Millmoor was partially restored in 2024 following a financial injection by Ken Booth Jr, the former Rotherham owner’s son.

Then 78, Booth Jr told the Rotherham Advertiser at the time: “The place was in a sad state. We had kids breaking in, trying to rip seats out, climbing the floodlight pylon, kicking a ball about.

“It was time for something to be done.”



Following restoration work, Millmoor was able to open its doors once again, with matches taking place on the hallowed turf.

Local junior teams were able to play there, relishing the opportunity to compete at a ground that first opened its doors in 1907 and that had housed a 25,170 crowd in its heyday.

In the summer of 2025 it was confirmed that Millmoor would become the new home of former WSL side Doncaster Belles.

This marked the return of regular senior football at the ground for the first time since 2008.



But it wasn’t to last… as in earlier this year the Booth family business went into administration.

CF Booth and its assets, including Millmoor, were subsequently acquired by the Ron Hull Group.

Following news of CF Booth’s demise, Doncaster Belles left Millmoor, moving to the SL2 Rail Stadium in Retford for the remainder of their season.

A statement by the Ron Hull Group, as shared by Rotherham Business News in May, read: “The buildings and structures selected in the current application to demolish are all in a poor condition due to years of neglect and are suffering from a general lack of maintenance, specifically elements like roof finishes and the structures themselves.



“It is assumed this situation accelerated in the period since Rotherham United football Club vacated the site.

“The current main stand is only partially completed, and has been exposed to the elements since at least 2007.

“The high cost of repair, yet alone proceed to complete this stand would be excessive given that there are very limited numbers of possible users of the ground. Thus meaning it is unbuyable.”

Plans submitted to local councillors involve demolishing the Millmoor Lane Stand and Railway Stand – in addition to removing pitch lighting columns and various other buildings.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If approved, demolition work is targeted to be completed by January next year.



It then remains to be seen what will become of the site, which meant so much to so many people for more than a century up to 2008.

Sports.title: UEFA nations could BOYCOTT World Cup in light of FIFA's plot to sell tournament
Sports.content:
UEFA nations could BOYCOTT World Cup in light of FIFA's plot to sell tournament

FIFA's decision to seek private investment has sent shockwaves through the football world and UEFA's members will meet this week to discuss their options in response

View 3 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino wants to bring in private investment (Image: Chris Brunskill/Getty Images)

European nations will discuss the possibility of boycotting the next World Cup in response to FIFA's controversial idea to seek private investment. FIFA's announcement on Tuesday has sent shockwaves through the football world - and efforts to stop the plans are now being plotted.

‌



World football's governing body says it wants to create a subsidiary worth $20billion (£15bn) and then sell off 20 per cent of FIFA Forward Enterprise to investors to raise $4.2bn (£3.16bn). If FIFA's members vote through the idea then Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, would lead the investors.

‌



During Gianni Infantino's time as president, FIFA has embarked upon a rapid commercialisation; FIFA is predicted to make $13billion (£9.6bn) in the four-year cycle up to 2026 - an increase of 72 per cent on the previous cycle. Infantino's expansionism has solidified his power, but it seems this step could be one too far.

‌



According to multiple reports, UEFA is organising an emergency meeting with its 55 members this week where they will plan their response. The Football Association was blindsided by FIFA's announcement and will join UEFA's members in deciding the next step.

A boycott of the next men's World Cup in 2030, which is set to be held across Spain, Morocco and Portugal, is one of the options on the table. The women's World Cup is next year in Brazil and could also be used as a threat to FIFA.

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

There is precedent for such a threat forcing FIFA to back down: in 2021 FIFA dropped a proposal to stage the World Cup every two years after UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin and his members said they wouldn't participate.

‌



View 3 Images Aleksander Ceferin will lead the pushback to FIFA's plans (Image: Getty Images)

Tuesday's bombshell has been compared by some to the European Super League debacle of 2021 when 12 clubs unsuccessfully tried to break away from UEFA to form a new competition. The backlash against FIFA's idea has been swift and forceful.

La Liga president Javier Tebas posted on X: "It doesn't seem like a reform. It seems like an electoral campaign financed with the future of football. Development cannot be used to buy votes or silences.

‌



"The competitions and commercial rights of FIFA are not the personal patrimony of Infantino. Whoever mixes politics, discipline, money, and power without transparency cannot lead anything. Infantino is not the solution to FIFA's governance. He is the problem. We are venturing deeper into the Iceberg and what remains to surface."

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino is facing a backlash (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

Football Supporters Europe said: “The World Cup is not for sale. Enough of this charade. FIFA member associations - and everyone who cares about the future of the game - must stand up to the man who wants to sell world football. Gianni Infantino must go.”

‌



Prime Minister Andy Burnham wrote on X: "Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

"The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will."

Sports.title: Liverpool’s dream final month of transfer window as Iraola reunion secured and Barcola signs
Sports.content:
Liverpool’s dream final month of transfer window as Iraola reunion secured and Barcola signs

Liverpool face a crucial few weeks in the transfer window with Andoni Iraola in need of both attacking and defensive reinforcements

View 5 Images Andoni Iraola desperately needs reinforcements (Image: Jacek Boczarski/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Liverpool need to find a replacement for Mohamed Salah and strengthen their defence before the new Premier League season begins. Following a tough campaign under Arne Slot, the Reds switched gears to Andoni Iraola and are aiming for a return to glory.

‌



Iraola's success at Bournemouth, culminating in the Cherries qualifying for European football for the first time, turned Liverpool heads. Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz have both signed deals at Anfield with Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate all leaving at the end of their contracts.

‌



The Spaniard will be well aware that he still needs positional upgrades before the new season starts, and the wing is a priority. At least two new signings are required if the Reds have any chance of reaching the heights they achieved in Slot's first season or Klopp's successful reign.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has detailed exactly what Liverpool should do to end their transfer window in the best way possible.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Federico Chiesa confirms Liverpool future stance and reveals new role under Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Sign a winger

Munoz was brought in for £34.5million last month in a deal structured over six years, amounting to just £5.75m annually. This means there remains a significant war chest to land a marquee winger, which is understood to be the Reds' biggest priority this summer.

‌



View 5 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's No. 1 target (Image: Sarah Stier - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

A number of wide players have been touted for a move to Anfield, but Bradley Barcola remains Liverpool's number one target. The Reds' bid to land the French international received a timely boost at the weekend when it emerged that Barcola had rejected a fresh contract offer from Paris Saint-Germain.

One stumbling block in securing a deal for the 23-year-old, however, is PSG's reported £140m asking price, which would set a club record. Liverpool are unwilling to match that figure and will reportedly seek a middle ground, with negotiations between the two sides said to continue this week.

‌



Should they manage to bring him in for a reduced fee, Iraola would have one of the most electrifying attackers in the world at his fingertips. Barcola possesses skill and pace in equal measure, equally capable of leading swift counter-attacks and unpicking stubborn defensive blocks.

View 5 Images Pedro Neto is another great option (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

His versatility to operate on either flank is an added bonus, affording the Reds boss the flexibility to deploy him on the left or slot him into Salah's role on the right. Should Liverpool fail to agree a lower price with PSG, however, Chelsea's Pedro Neto could be a worthy fallback option.

‌



Chelsea are not actively pursuing Neto's sale but the Portuguese would command a lower fee than Barcola, while still representing a versatile and Premier League-proven addition across the forward line.

Boost the defence

After securing a wide forward, Liverpool must shift their focus to their struggling defence. Even prior to Konate's departure, the Reds were light at the back, considering Joe Gomez's persistent time on the sidelines and Giovanni Leoni's lengthy recovery from an ACL injury.

The situation appears even more problematic now following Gomez's withdrawal due to injury in the pre-season friendly against Sunderland at the weekend, while new signing Jacquet was omitted as a precaution.

‌



View 5 Images Joe Gomez's injury spells trouble for Liverpool (Image: Ian Horrocks/Sunderland AFC via Getty Images)

If doubts exist over whether Liverpool possess sufficient depth before the campaign has even started, it suggests something is fundamentally amiss. Iraola acknowledged as much last Monday, when he delivered his second press conference and the opening one of Liverpool's summer 2026 pre-season tour of the USA.

The manager referenced right-back Conor Bradley's own rehabilitation from a serious injury and emphasised that, while he views Bradley as the club's long-term right-back, the club are seeking a "solution" to their centre-back and right-back concerns. As a result, it would be smart to recruit a defender capable of performing both roles to a high standard, as Liverpool's extensive list of injured defenders continues their recovery.

‌



Pursuing James Hill appears to be the most logical move for Iraola, given the defender flourished under him at Bournemouth last season. Across 29 league outings, Hill proved to be one of the Cherries' most reliable figures at the back.

While predominantly a centre-back, he made three appearances at right-back - a versatility that suits Liverpool well, given Iraola has identified Bradley as the long-term first choice in that position. Hill registered 11.16 defensive contributions per 90 minutes, won 65.5% of his aerial duels, and came out on top in 63.8% of his overall duels.

No central defender in the league won more aerial duels per 90 minutes than Hill (4.88), and he also showcased an ability to drive the ball in the forward-thinking manner Iraola wants from his defence, crafting an impressive 0.56 chances per 90.

‌



View 5 Images Andoni Iraola could bring James Hill to Anfield (Image: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

At present, there is virtually no chatter surrounding a potential exit from the Vitality Stadium. But that is precisely something Liverpool ought to change by stepping up their interest.

He would represent a vital addition to the squad, bolstering depth and filling a homegrown slot in the Reds' domestic and European squads.

Article continues below

With Hill and Barcola brought on board, Liverpool could head into the new season with genuine confidence in a near-unassailable squad - one capable of bouncing back from recent setbacks and striking fear into their rivals.

Sports.title: Not Man Utd or Liverpool – this is who fans are backing most to win the Premier League
Sports.content:
Not Man Utd or Liverpool – this is who fans are backing most to win the Premier League

Manchester United and Liverpool enter the new Premier League campaign under the guidance of new permanent bosses but don't feature among the most heavily backed teams to win the title

View 2 Images Arsenal are targeting back-to-back Premier League titles come 2027 (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Premier League fans are hard at work casting their predictions for who will come out on top of the 2026/27 title race. But Manchester United and Liverpool remain outside picks for the crown despite major changes this summer.

‌



Michael Carrick has been handed the permanent reins at Old Trafford, while Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. Manchester City also reached the end of an era after Pep Guardiola concluded his 10-year tenure at the Etihad, with Enzo Maresca named his successor.

‌



However, punters are largely going with consistency above all else as Arsenal have emerged as the public's favourite to retain their crown. Mikel Arteta's men finally ended a 22-year search for another league title last season.

‌



According to wagers taken by bet365 up until now, the Gunners account for 34.4 per cent of all outright title-winner odds placed. That's perhaps to be expected given Arteta's side are the outright favourites to retain the trophy at odds of 6/4.

Despite only just avoiding relegation to the Championship last term, Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham have been backed by 4.3 per cent of bettors. That's likely thanks to much more appealing odds of 20/1, though their £237m transfer market spree, adding Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke, Andrew Robertson and Marcos Senesi to their ranks, will have helped.

Sports.title: Matheus Cunha put on notice at Man Utd as exciting transfer sealed
Sports.content:
Matheus Cunha put on notice at Man Utd as exciting transfer sealed

Manchester United have a couple of new faces in attack, which could spell bad news for Matheus Cunha

View 3 Images Matheus Cunha has been put on notice (Image: Getty Images)

Matheus Cunha has already shown why Manchester United spent big to bring him to Old Trafford. But the Brazilian's biggest strength has also highlighted one of Michael Carrick's lingering problems.

‌



Cunha offers craft, technical quality and clever movement in the final third, yet he is not the kind of explosive winger capable of leaving defenders trailing over long distances. That lack of outright pace was something United struggled with throughout last season, particularly when trying to stretch compact defences or launch quick counterattacks.

‌



Carrick's side still needs that dimension, but the head coach may now have two answers at his disposal. One is a familiar face in Marcus Rashford, who appears set to return to Old Trafford after an unsuccessful bid to secure a permanent move to Barcelona. The other is exciting teenage signing Tynan Thompson, whose biggest asset is his blistering speed.

‌



Although United's new-look front three of Benjamin Sesko, Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo has shown plenty of promise, one obvious weakness still stands out - a lack of outright pace on the flanks. That issue is most noticeable down the left side, where Cunha has featured for the majority of pre-season.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd stance on hijacking Chelsea's Danny Welbeck transfer after secret talks READ MORE :

Man Utd star takes drastic action as Ruben Amorim plots transfer reunion READ MORE :

The former Wolves star enjoyed a productive first campaign at Old Trafford, scoring 10 goals and supplying four assists. There is little doubt he has justified his arrival. However, his strengths lie in his technical quality, creativity and intelligent movement rather than explosive pace, meaning United still lack genuine speed threat in wide areas.

‌



As a result, Carrick's side sometimes struggled when matches became stretched, lacking someone capable of making penetrating runs beyond the defence and exploiting open space. That, however, may be about to change.

Rashford is one player who could solve that problem. The forward looked set for a permanent switch to Barcelona, but after the Spanish champions spent £70million on Anthony Gordon instead, Rashford's hopes of remaining in Catalonia appear dashed.

Should he remain at Old Trafford beyond the summer, Rashford would hand Carrick qualities that very few of his forwards possess - electric speed, direct dribbling and an ability to push opposition back lines deeper. Rashford is hardly a new face at United, but because Carrick did not work with him last season, his return would effectively provide the head coach with a fresh tactical option.

‌



View 3 Images Marcus Rashford could be exactly what Michael Carrick needs to improve his attack (Image: 2020 Soccrates Images B.V.)

United also have another rapid attacker in the shape of new arrival Tynan Thompson. The 18-year-old winger completed his move from Tottenham earlier this month in a transfer worth an initial £4million, with another £4million included in performance-related add-ons.

Whether Thompson becomes part of Carrick's senior squad this season remains uncertain, but his lightning pace and eagerness to attack defenders make him an exciting talent. Like Rashford, he brings a contrasting profile and could supply the penetration United occasionally lacked throughout the previous campaign.

‌



His arrival bears comparison with Ayden Heaven's move in January 2025. The central defender joined from Arsenal's academy as an 18-year-old for £1.5million and has since gone on to make 24 first-team appearances.

View 3 Images Tynan Thompson completed a move to Manchester United earlier this month (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Thompson, an England youth international, scored 13 goals and provided six assists across Tottenham's Under-18 and Under-21 sides last season. Seven of those goals came in just seven UEFA Youth League appearances.

‌



The teenager became United's first attacking addition of the summer. Before his arrival, the club's transfer business had been centred on reinforcing midfield, with Chelsea's Andrey Santos and Aston Villa's Youri Tielemans both joining earlier this month.

United had also been closing in on Atalanta midfielder Ederson after reaching an agreement for the Brazilian, only for the deal to collapse before completion. Attention has since turned towards alternative midfield targets, with AS Roma's Manu Kone and Brighton's Carlos Baleba both reported to be under consideration.

Although much of the club's focus has been on strengthening the centre of the pitch, United are looking to continue bolstering their front line ahead of the new season, leaving stars like Cunha under pressure to retain their place in the starting XI.
