“It is going to be a tough second season, we know that, but we feel there is more to come from the existing group. It was difficult last season with a lot of players coming in later and having to relocate to the area and settle as the season started, but they were great for us and I feel there is more to come this season.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s back’: Zinedine Zidane named France head coach in long-awaited homecoming
Sports.content:
For Tuesday’s front page, L’Équipe simply went with “Il revient” – “He’s back” – echoing the newspaper’s 2005 headline when Zinedine Zidane came out of international retirement. At the time, the midfielder’s upcoming return was seen as a major boost to Les Bleus’ ailing World Cup qualifying campaign. There was a similar sense of anticipation now as the roads around the French Football Federation headquarters in Paris were closed off for Zidane’s unveiling as head coach. A crowd of France fans had gathered outside by the overground Métro tracks with flags, flares and drums, as more than a hundred journalists and TV cameras were ushered into the building.

The fact that Zidane would be next in line to lead France after Didier Deschamps had been an open secret for several years and by the end of the World Cup his arrival was all but confirmed. The new head coach entered the press conference room on Tuesday morning only minutes after his appointment was confirmed by the FFF’s executive committee, but the feeling in France was that the occasion was a couple of decades in the making.

“It’s a new cycle,” the FFF president, Philippe Diallo, said after a preamble in which he paid tribute to Deschamps’ 14-year tenure. Talks with the 1998 World Cup hero, Diallo said, began in February 2025, the month after Deschamps announced he would step down this summer. “Zinedine Zidane is one of the legends of French football and he had made it known that it was one of his dreams to manage the French national team,” Diallo said. “We wanted someone with the aura, the ability, and the hearts of our fans and the French people to manage what is one of the best national teams in the world.”

View image in fullscreen France supporters gather in Paris to celebrate the confirmation of one of the greatest players in Les Bleus’ history as their new head coach. Photograph: Teresa Suárez/EPA

For Zidane, this announcement was the culmination of nearly half a decade of waiting in the wings. “I had several offers from clubs in the last four to five years, but I turned them all down for France,” the former Real Madrid manager said. “The national team is the only thing I wanted. I’ve been with the French teams since I was a kid, all the way up to the senior team. I’m a bit emotional. You might not be able to tell, but I am incredibly excited.”

Zidane declared it was the greatest day of his managerial career. “It’s an immense joy. I am ready for the challenge.”

The five years that have passed since the end of Zidane’s second spell in Madrid will have been spent preparing to take over Les Bleus. “I’ve been watching France as a supporter, but also as a future manager. I don’t think there are any traps. It’s new to me, but I’m not scared. This is what I wanted.” The 54-year-old’s first public appearance as head coach was light on the details of his plans for the national team. He notably sidestepped a question about whether Kylian Mbappé would retain the armband, insisting that he would have to meet the team and its “extraordinary players” first of all. “We need to keep this team winning,” he said, adding that he was impressed with what he had seen during the World Cup.

“I was a No 10 in my playing days,” he said when asked about the style of play he would look to implement. Whether his answer implies a continuation of Deschamps’ attacking shift remains to be seen, but his answers did hint at some kind of change of direction. “Laurent [Blanc] was Laurent, Didier was Didier, and Zizou is Zizou,” he said playfully.

One of Zidane’s long-term objectives will be to compete with the reigning world champions, who have now beaten France in three consecutive tournament semi‑finals. “I spent 25 years in Spain and you know what that means,” he said, before pointing out that the task ahead went beyond beating La Roja. “I know Spanish football very well, but they won’t be the only opponents. You have to beat all of the teams.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was sent off by Horazio Elizondo for butting Italy’s Marco Materazzi in the chest in the 2006 World Cup final. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Zidane’s four-year contract will begin next month, with his extended staff to be unveiled a few weeks before the first internationals of the new season. “We’ll see each other again in September to talk about it. It’s a good thing that we’ll have three weeks with the players.” The focus for now, Zidane said, is on his first match in charge, which will be in Turkey on 25 September.

His homecoming, meanwhile, will be against Italy, just over 20 years after his dramatic exit from the international stage. If the raucous reception as he stepped out of the FFF headquarters is anything to go by, it will be one of the more memorable evenings in the Stade de France’s history.

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini returns as Italy head coach with Claudio Ranieri named technical director
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini has agreed to be Italy head coach for a second time, the president of the Italian Football ​Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malagò, said on Tuesday, also confirming Claudio Ranieri would take over as technical director.

Mancini replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who ⁠left the post in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession, and returns to a job he held between 2018 and 2023. He led the national team to European Championship glory in 2021 with a penalty shootout victory over England at Wembley but then failed to reach the 2022 World Cup and a slow start to Euro 2024 qualifying. In total, Mancini managed Italy for 58 matches during his first spell and at club level has managed Inter, Fiorentina and Manchester City, where he spent three years and guided them to their first Premier League title in 2011-12.

“Mancini is the coach,” Malago ‌said on Tuesday. “I believed that the best person to become head coach was ‌Roberto Mancini.”

The former FIGC technical director ‌Paolo Maldini and his adviser, Leonardo, resigned from their roles on Monday after Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as head coach was blocked because of the former midfielder’s ties to a Russian betting firm. Pep Guardiola was the association’s first choice but turned down the job last month.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ranieri replaces ⁠Maldini. The 74-year-old, who led Leicester City to the Premier League title in ​2016, will oversee technical operations and ​elite football development across Italy’s national team structures. “I needed someone with ​whom I could share ‌the decision on ​the coach, because ​without that shared view my reasoning would have carried little weight,” Malago said. “So consequently, we have a new coach and a new technical director for Italy.”

Sports.title: Chelsea close in on signing of Danny Welbeck - as Xabi Alonso prepares to allow up to three strikers to leave the club this summer
Sports.content:
Chelsea are finalising a two-year deal for Danny Welbeck, with the Brighton & Hove Albion striker set to undergo a medical before potentially linking up with his new club in Hong Kong.

Daily Mail Sport revealed three days ago how Xabi Alonso’s side had suddenly shown interest in Welbeck, who, at 35 years old, would bring significant experience into the Blues’ squad. Jordan Henderson, 36 and at Brentford, is also a transfer target.

Welbeck, who scored 13 Premier League goals last season, is in line to sign terms until 2028 at Stamford Bridge. If all goes to plan, he will link up with his new team-mates on their pre-season in Hong Kong, before further stops in Malaysia and Indonesia. He had 12 months remaining on his contract at Brighton.

Alonso and his squad are currently in Sydney, Australia for their pre-season tour but they will be moving on to Hong Kong this weekend after their next friendly versus Tottenham.

Chelsea have tweaked their transfer approach this summer by targeting more ‘ready-made’ players who are older than those they currently have.

Danny Welbeck is close to agreeing his move to Chelsea from Brighton

Liam Delap is one of up to three strikers Chelsea may let move on this summer

Alonso originally targeted the signing of Granit Xhaka, 33, but Sunderland refused to sell their captain. They also looked at bringing in John Stones as a 32-year-old free agent.

Maxence Lacroix, 26 and from Crystal Palace, is close to being confirmed for £52million. Morgan Rogers, the 24-year-old from Aston Villa, has also signed for £117m.

The arrival of Welbeck should lead to other movements in the striker department at Chelsea. Alonso already has Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Nicolas Jackson, Marc Guiu and Joao Pedro on the books. At least two of those five should be sold or loaned, and possibly three.

Joao Pedro is considered untouchable and not for sale. He scored a nine-minute hat-trick in their 6-4 friendly victory over Western Sydney Wanderers. Delap struggled in that win, though he was surrounded mainly by academy products while on the pitch, whereas Joao Pedro was substituted on along with the A team.

When asked about Welbeck after that friendly win, Alonso said: ‘No comment.’

Sports.title: Football must rally against Gianni Infantino's brazen bid to put World Cup up for sale - this is the most blatant ambush to disfigure sport imaginable, writes JONATHAN McEVOY
Sports.content:
It can now never be contradicted that Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump share a bone-deep appreciation of all that it means to best serve the world’s oldest and most popular game. Namely, the pursuit of money.

This endeavour has proved itself an enduringly compelling sport since the apple fell in the Garden, so it is as old as sin itself, and a pastime that today endangers bastardising modern football more deeply than any of the bank-lining panjandrums who went before them could ever have envisaged.

My goodness, others have tried hard to pollute sport. Juan Antonio Samaranch, the old Spanish fascist who sold the International Olympic Committee’s flaunted reputation for sporting purity all those years ago, gave it a good heave.

His self-acclaimed Excellency was reputed not to have earned a salary for his services in the name of progressing a vision set by the modern Olympics’ founding father Pierre de Coubertin. But in fawned-to, limousine-conveying grandeur he sold out his inheritance to dubious courtiers who militated against an ethic centred on guaranteeing a fair playing field for the youth of the world.

The youth of the world! Ha, if you will. The Olympic hymn, white doves at opening ceremonies, the oath sworn by an athlete on behalf of his fellow competitors in the name of honest competition. It was a pledge best uttered by the well-meaning, co-opted liar with crossed fingers behind his or her back.

We are, alas, inured to such hokum, a reality that reached its public apogee of infamy when Ben Johnson ran like a god in Seoul and was exposed as not quite the clock-defying deity we had hoped him to be.

Football needs to rebel against Gianni Infantino's (left) bid to sell the World Cup

Lance Armstrong, East Germany’s state-sponsored doping, the Fuentes drugs scandal in Spain, and so the list goes on. Indeed, WG Grace, cricket’s founding father, was no stranger to sharp practices in the Victorian Age. Old as sin itself, as we were saying, long before Allen Stanford, the Texan fraudster, promised huge, ill-begotten riches to cricket or LIV golf’s accumulators entered the stage with their distorting avarice bankrolled by Middle Eastern riyals.

Sport being traduced from within is endemic. Yet, we must still rail against this latest and unprecedented news, a departure in its arching scope, of Infantino effectively putting the World Cup itself up for sale to the highest bidder.

This when his chief elected responsibility as the head of FIFA, football’s world governing body and its supposed guarantor, is to preserve the verities of the game from malign speculators.

It is the most blatant and brazen ambush to disfigure sport in elected office imaginable.

To get back to Trump, and his recent phone call to Monaco-domiciled Infantino that represented the nadir of a largely successful World Cup. It all becomes clear, now.

We are speaking about the word Trump dripped into Infantino’s ear in his successful intervention to overturn US striker Folarin Balogun’s automatic one-match suspension. Political neutrality, a sine qua non of FIFA, was waved aside.

Infantino ludicrously claimed: ‘Potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide. It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.’

Trump scoffed at criticism of his meddling. ‘I understand sports well,’ the president bloviated, while admitting from the Oval Office that he did not know what a red card or its implications for a non-negotiable ban implied.

It is the most blatant and brazen ambush to disfigure sport in elected office imaginable

Infantino doubled down this week, opining: ‘To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 per cent safety and security, only joy and happiness.’

Thanks, Gianni. The dots can be joined now. Who is lined up to be a major investor in the scheme to sell shares in the World Cup to private investors? None other than Joshua Kushner, brother of Trump’s in-law Jared, a key agitator in taking the World Cup to America.

Trump and Infantino, who gave the former the bogus bauble of a peace prize, never awarded before and likely never to be awarded again, are in cahoots, hence the smoke they blow up each other’s posterior. US bank JPMorgan is also cited as a willing owner.

Under Infantino’s scheme, a company would be established to control the men’s and women’s World Cups and the Club World Cup. Which brings us to the point about money and what Infantino would be set to earn as a result of his brainchild.

All bosses of sporting bodies think a lot about this, their personal riches. They do not earn as much as the star performers, mostly men, accrue in the sport they (the governors) ‘serve’.

This disparity rankles. They want to get as rich as they can and seek to devise ways to do so.

So Infantino would, as it is understood, take on the role of ‘commissioner’ of his new World Cup order once his stint as FIFA president expires in 2031, offering him the potential to earn £37.5million a year, a some tenfold increase on his current wages. He will no doubt talk of wanting to grow the game. This is part of the playbook you would expect. He butters up the 211 members/sycophants who buttress his position – he will stand unopposed in office – by offering these supplicants shares in his folly, worth £15million to sell as they wish. That is nice earning possibilities for backwater associations if they then sublet their stakes.

And then we have the grotesque spectre of World Cups being staged more regularly than every four years, a dilution of world sport’s premier event, as all the moolah-grabbers look to exploit television rights deals, sponsorship, (exorbitant) ticket prices and hospitality sales on a more regular basis.

Joshua Kushner (pictured), brother of Trump’s in-law Jared, is lined up to be a major investor

The old framework of four-yearly World Cups would be swept away, just as wantonly as ‘hydration breaks’ were introduced spuriously over the last few weeks, with their advertising allure to TV networks clear.

Four quarters, rather than two halves, was a notion mooted, by the way, by Sepp Blatter ahead of the previous World Cup in America in 1994.

This latest abhorrence is of a different order. This, as Joseph Conrad wrote of another unchecked empire, is ‘a flabby, pretending, weak-eyed devil of a rapacious and pitiless folly’.

The emphasis is on greed, and football should rise up against it.

Sports.title: Man United youngsters
Sports.content:
As opportunity knocks for a number of Manchester United’s academy stars in pre-season, only the chosen few will be part of the first-team squad once the new Premier League campaign gets underway.

United are open to the majority of the Under 21s who have featured in the opening friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg going out on loan to further their development, with the exception of players like Shea Lacey, Jack and Tyler Fletcher and rising star JJ Gabriel.

For several youngsters who have been on the first-team fringes for some time now, the move could be permanent after the club made a decision on their futures this week.

Goalkeeper Radek Vitek, left back Harry Amass and midfielders Dan Gore and Toby Collyer all spent last season out on loan and have been told they are unlikely to feature for United this season either.

In the case of Vitek and Amass, United are prepared to sell both players or consider another loan with an option to buy. Until then, both players will remain part of the first-team squad and train at Carrington.

Czech keeper Vitek, who has played more minutes than anyone against Wrexham and Rosenborg, is a target for Middlesbrough and a host of other Championship clubs after starring on loan at Bristol City last season.

Michael Carrick has given a lot of game time to his young academy stars in pre-season

A host of United youngsters got a runout in Norway, including Shea Lacey (front left), Harry Amass (centre) and 15-year-old JJ Gabriel (back right)

Amass played in both games and got a goal and an assist against Rosenborg. He is valued at around £6million after spending last season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich.

With United still in the market for a third central midfielder after paying a combined £85m to sign Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, Gore and Collyer are believed to have been told that their best hope of regular football next season will be with the Under 21s.

Hull City retain an interest in re-signing Collyer following his loan there last season, and Gore is available again after a successful loan spell at Rotherham.

There is no shortage of other United youngsters looking to impress in the remaining four pre-season games against Atletico Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain, Leeds and AC Milan, even though opportunities may be harder to come by as United’s World Cup stars return to action.

The club are famed for their youth system, and a feature of United’s first two pre-season games has been how well the academy players seized their opportunity in Helsinki and Trondheim.

Lacey scored United’s opening goal over Rosenborg on Friday after he was named in the starting line-up, and Jaydan Kamason starred with two assists when Michael Carrick brought on the kids in the second half and they stretched the lead to 5-0.

United's first-team stars will be looking over their shoulder with so much talent waiting in the wings

In the first game against Wrexham, the academy side played more fluent football than the seniors who went 1-0 down before half-time, but United couldn’t find the equaliser their performance deserved.

Lacey will be looking to kick on after making his first-team breakthrough last season along with the Fletcher twins, and Gabriel is edging ever closer to a debut. Jim Thwaites is also understood to be particularly highly-rated by Carrick and his coaching staff even though he hasn’t played yet.

Here Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the exciting youngsters knocking on the first-team door.

SHEA LACEY

The only outfield player from the academy to make the starting line-up against Rosenborg, Lacey justified his inclusion with a well-taken goal just after the half-hour mark to set United on their way to a comprehensive victory.

The 19-year-old from Liverpool is predominantly a right winger but demonstrated his versatility in Trondheim by playing in the No 10 role and drifting wide to link up play.

Lacey’s star quality was underlined when Thomas Tuchel called him up to train with the England senior squad in October, and he made his first two appearances for United before being sent off on his Old Trafford debut against Brighton in the FA Cup.

He re-appeared at Brighton in the Premier League on the final day of the season, though, and we will undoubtedly be seeing more of him this term.

Lacey made four first-team appearances last season, including three in the Premier League

Lacey saw red on his Old Trafford debut in the FA Cup against Brighton for throwing the ball away in a show of dissent

JACK FLETCHER

The older of the Fletcher twins – who joined United from Manchester City for a joint fee of around £1.25m three years ago – Jack was named in the starting line-up for the Wrexham game and performed well in the No 10 role before Carrick made wholesale changes at half-time.

He and Tyler play in central midfield, but they are expected to stay at United this season despite the club’s £85m investment in Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, and plans to sign a third midfielder.

Jack is seen as a more creative player and tends to operate further forward, although the England youth international can also be used as a right winger or full back.

The 19-year-old made three first-team appearances last season and will be aiming to add more this term.

Jack Fletcher tends to operate further forward in midfield but can also be used as a right winger or full back

TYLER FLETCHER

He didn’t start against Wrexham but at least had the distinction of captaining United’s younger XI in the second half in Helsinki, before coming on as a substitute along with his brother when Carrick made changes after an hour against Rosenborg.

This could be a big season for Tyler after he made his senior international debut for Scotland in a friendly against Bolivia last month and then got a late call-up for the World Cup following an injury to Billy Gilmour.

Like Lacey, he played for United at Brighton on the last day of the season in May, and those two are understood to be at the front of the queue for first-team opportunities this year.

Tyler Fletcher had the distinction of captaining United’s younger XI in the second half in Helsinki against Wrexham

JJ GABRIEL

The most eagerly anticipated appearance in pre-season is likely to be made by the young man who doesn’t turn 16 until October.

Gabriel was included in United’s squad for the first time for the trip to Norway last week, but was one of only three players from the 25-man party not to get on the pitch.

It’s only a matter of time before the player dubbed Kid Messi gets his chance, after Premier League rules prevented United from naming him in their squad last season because he was only 14 when it began.

Gabriel still made an impression, though, as he was called up to first-team training in the autumn and starred for the Under 18s with 29 goals in 32 appearances to win the Under 18s Premier League player of the season award. Expect to hear a lot more about this boy.

JJ Gabriel has only just turned 15 but could be in line for a Premier League debut this season

JAYDAN KAMASON

The England youth international was United’s standout performer in the second half against Rosenborg, getting forward down the right flank to set up goals for Harry Amass and Ethan Williams.

Kamason struggled with injuries last season but is hoping to have more luck this term, and has certainly made a promising start in pre-season.

The 19-year-old is prepared to go out on loan to further his development, but has his sights locked firmly on a career at Old Trafford.

‘If I need a few loans or whatever, we'll have to see, but I'm trying to get to that top level – and that's Manchester United. You have to be ambitious,’ he said after the game in Trondheim.

Jaydan Kamason struggled with injuries last season but is hoping to have more luck this term, and has certainly made a promising start in pre-season

JIM THWAITES

Although he has been left on the bench for both pre-season games so far, Thwaites is said to be particularly highly regarded among the current crop of Under 21s.

A gifted midfielder and dead-ball specialist, the 18-year-old has seized his opportunity to train with the senior squad since Ruben Amorim first invited him in, and was rewarded by Carrick for his performance during the training camp in Dublin in April with a place on the bench at Chelsea.

With United strengthening in midfield, they have to make a decision about whether to keep Thwaites or send him out on loan after a planned move in January was scuppered by injury.

Jim Thwaites is a dead-ball specialist and is particularly highly regarded among the current crop of Under 21s

JACOB DEVANEY

Devaney has come off the bench to play in central defence in both pre-season games despite preferring a midfield role, and got on the scoresheet against Rosenborg with United’s third goal from a corner shortly after replacing Ayden Heaven.

The 19-year-old excelled as a midfielder on loan at St Mirren during a difficult season for the Scottish club, and is ready to head out again if it boosts his hopes of playing for United.

Jacob Devaney struck for United in their 5-0 pre-season friendly win over Rosenborg in Norway last week

‘The main aim for me is to play for Manchester United week in, week out,’ said the Republic of Ireland Under 21s international in Trondheim.

‘Obviously, I want to play first-team football. So whether that is at United, learning from the best for the next year, or if I have to go on loan again and gain more valuable experience, that's what I'll do.’

PS: Not all the young players knocking on the first-team door at United this season will have come through the club’s academy.

There is great excitement around teenager winger Tynan Thompson who has moved to Old Trafford from Tottenham in a deal worth £4m plus £4m in add-ons.

Thompson will be part of the senior group at Carrington, but the 18-year-old hasn’t trained with them yet and it’s too early to tell if he will feature in pre-season as United’s World Cup contingent continue to report back.

Sports.title: Why Bradley Barcola is the perfect fit for Andoni Iraola: How 'the grasshopper' will take Liverpool to new heights, the secrets to his relentless chance creation and proof the £140m bargain solves huge problem
Sports.content:
Why Bradley Barcola is the perfect fit for Andoni Iraola: How 'the grasshopper' will take Liverpool to new heights, the secrets to his relentless chance creation and proof the £140m bargain solves huge problem

Unlock more from our team inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

So much for keeping your cards close to your chest. When new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was asked recently where he needed to strengthen, he replied: ‘We definitely need to sign a winger.’

When you have to replace one of the greatest players in your club’s history in Mo Salah, and your out-and-out right-wing options during a pre-season tour of the US are Kieran Morrison, 19, and Joshua Abe, 16, there's not much point pretending otherwise. Especially when the new guy in charge is renowned for his fast, direct, attacking style of football.

Liverpool know the man they want to fill that obvious hole, too. As Daily Mail Sport reported over the weekend, the club are working on a deal to sign 23-year-old winger Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG, however, want around £140million for the France international, which would smash the British record of £125m Liverpool forked out for Alexander Isak last summer.

A fair old whack for a player who’s stalled over a new contract, told PSG he wants to leave, and had fallen down the pecking order under Luis Enrique anyway, with Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia his preferred wide options during the business end of the Champions League. So, you imagine there might be some wriggle room.

Yet this is also the young star who, essentially, replaced Kylian Mbappe on PSG’s flank when he joined Real Madrid two years ago. Club legend Javier Pastore has said Barcola could reach Mbappe’s level one day, too.

Even though his minutes became limited, Barcola ranked behind only team-mate Ousmane Dembele and Monaco’s Ansu Fati for expected goals and assists per 90 minutes in Ligue 1 last season. In other words, he's a chance-creating machine.

Liverpool are being quoted around £140m - a Premier League record fee - to sign PSG winger Bradley Barcola

Barcola replaced Kylian Mbappe on PSG’s flank when he joined Real Madrid two years ago - and club legend Javier Pastore has said he could reach Mbappe’s level one day, too

Barcola played in all eight of France’s games at the World Cup, starting four of them. He scored three goals and set up another.

His speed, tricks and flicks on the ball won him the nickname la sauterelle, or the grasshopper, as he came through the ranks at Lyon, though he was never one of those generational wonderkids pegged for superstardom from the moment they kick a ball.

‘He was a normal kid, he never played above his age category, never jumped a stage,’ Lyon’s former academy manager Jean-Francois Vulliez once told Sky Sports. ‘His maturation was a normal process.’

Barcola joined Lyon, an academy famed for producing players like Alexandre Lacazette, Rayan Cherki and Karim Benzema, aged eight after being spotted playing in an indoor tournament for hometown club AS Buers Villeurbanne.

One of six siblings, Barcola’s brother Malcolm, a goalkeeper, also played for Lyon. His mum played when she was younger, too. ‘It’s rare but she’s the one who gave us the passion,’ Bradley once said.

Barcola and his brother watched clips she had filmed of their matches in the living room and, at weekends, his dad would take them to the local stadium to practise.

‘My father made Bradley do specific work in front of goal, and me, as a goalkeeper… he made me work too,’ Malcolm told Le Progres. ‘We complemented each other well.’

Barcola has six goals in 28 caps for France since making his debut in 2024

He scored three goals at the World Cup, including one against England in the third-place play-off

And yet it so nearly didn’t happen. Barcola’s career was stalling at Lyon under Laurent Blanc.

He was struggling to break into the first team and his coaches at the time could see he wasn’t putting the effort in during training, nor scoring the goals to justify his selection. In January 2023, he came close to being sent out on loan to Swiss side St Gallen.

But they just felt there was something there. And when team-mate Karl Toko Ekambi stormed down the tunnel after being substituted, was jeered by the fans, filmed booting a rubbish bin in fury, and never played for the club again, Barcola's chance came.

He scored five goals and set up nine more in the back end of the 2022-23 season, including the winner at the Parc des Princes against a PSG side that would spend £40m on the then 20-year-old that summer.

You can see why Liverpool think he’s the right fit, too. For a start, he’s rapid. Barcola was the fifth quickest player in the Champions League last season and the seventh fastest at the World Cup.

Raw pace, especially across the forward line, is something Liverpool sorely lack.

Iraola has always wanted his teams to get the ball forward as quickly as possible.

Bournemouth mustered the most direct attacks of any team last season, the joint-most goals from counter-attacks and, across Iraola’s entire reign, attacked the fastest (1.95 metres per second) of all Premier League sides while averaging the second-fewest passes per sequence. Barcola’s pace would be a huge weapon.

It’s not just his runs in behind, either. One of Barcola’s favourite tricks is to knock the ball past his defender from a standing start and then leave him for dead, or even to race back to his own goal to collect the ball, then take a touch, turn his man and go in the blink of an eye.

Nor is he just a chalk-on-your-boots wide man, which also plays into the Iraola plan. Barcola would often drift into the channels to allow PSG’s stampeding full backs to provide the width ahead of him.

Having played as a striker until the age of 17, Barcola has always had a nose for goal.

Barcola boasted, by some distance, the most shot-ending carries per 90 minutes of anyone in Ligue 1. Despite only playing 1,750 minutes, his total of 40 put him behind only Mason Greenwood (43), who played nearly 2,500 minutes.

His 1.9 chances created from open play per 90 minutes also put him behind only team-mates Dembele and Lee Kang-In across the league.

He can play on both wings, as he did in each leg of their Champions League last 16 demolition of Chelsea, and often found himself taking up central positions.

The screengrabs below come just before he scored in both legs, with his full backs high up the pitch in wide areas.

Barcola took up a central position on the shoulder of Chelsea's right-sided centre back Wesley Fofana before opening the scoring in their Champions League tie in March

He repeated the trick in the second leg, drifting in from the right this time much to the concern of left centre back Jorrel Hato

His combined touch map (below) from PSG's entire successful Champions League campaign shows just how central he often played.

Barcola’s combined touch map for Champions League matches in 2025-26 reveals how often he drifted inside

And even in Ligue 1, most of his shots and goals came from central positions inside the penalty area.

He carries the goal threat and positional nous of a conventional striker.

Barcola’s shots (white) and goals (red) in Ligue 1 in 2025-26 (the bigger the circle, the bigger the chance in terms of xG)

That, too, would fit into Iraola’s usual style. Flying full backs were a crucial part of Bournemouth’s tactical plan. In the 2024-25 season, before his move to Liverpool last summer, Milos Kerkez was one of the most attacking defenders in the division.

Iraola has a track record of getting the best from his wingers, who play more as inside forwards.

Antoine Semenyo flourished under him before joining Manchester City. He worked wonders with Isi Palazon at Rayo Vallecano.

In Barcola, he could inherit another. This one, however, might just cost a bit more.

Sports.title: Shirtless Tom Brady enjoys family vacation to Alaska as NFL icon and his three children pose with sled dogs and go fishing on 'trip of a lifetime'
Sports.content:
Shirtless Tom Brady enjoys family vacation to Alaska as NFL icon and his three children pose with sled dogs and go fishing on 'trip of a lifetime'

Tom Brady and his three children enjoyed 'the trip of a lifetime' in Alaska in recent days as the NFL icon posted a series of loving pictures from their vacation.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner, 48, posted a flurry of images from the fun-filled trip on Instagram on Tuesday.

Brady flew west with his daughter Vivian, 13, and sons Jack, 18 and Benjamin, 16, for a few days of adventure in the outdoors.

The pictures show the Brady clan enjoying a trip with a pack of sled dogs, while they also went fishing in lakes and were brave enough to go swimming in the icy water overlooked by stunning mountains.

Brady made sure to get a snap of his ripped physique within the post as he bravely took off his shirt and jumped off the side of a boat into the bitterly cold water.

'A week in Alaska with my three best friends. The trip of a lifetime,' Brady wrote in his caption, along with a heart emoji.

Tom Brady and his three children enjoyed 'the trip of a lifetime' in Alaska in recent days

Brady bravely took of his shirt and jumped off the side of a boat into the bitterly cold water

The seven-time Super Bowl champion poses with sons Jack and Benjamin on a boat

It continued what has been a busy summer for Brady. He attended Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's lavish New York City wedding earlier this month, watched plenty of World Cup action and even squeezed in a golf trip to Ireland with his dad.

But the legendary quarterback has also attracted plenty of criticism in recent weeks for starting a dramatic feud with Logan Paul.

Amid the spectacle of the World Cup final between champions Spain and Argentina in New York, the NFL legend flipped his middle finger at Paul in the latest stunt.

A day earlier Brady slapped YouTuber-turned-wrestler Paul at a Fanatics Fest event in New York. The saga began with the pair's flag football 'feud' earlier this year.

A source suggested to The Daily Mail that the 'feud' with Brady and Paul is 'expected to eventually spill over into the WWE ring' at some point in the future.

Many fear Brady, 48, is having a midlife crisis, amplified by the wounds of his divorce from supermodel Gisele Bundchen in 2022 after 13 years of marriage.

Things are only going to get busier for the former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star when the new NFL season gets underway in a matter of weeks.

Brady is poised to enter the third year of his decade-long, $375 million contract as Fox's lead NFL color commentator.

He's also juggling his responsibilities as a minority owner with the Las Vegas Raiders and, on Tuesday, his head coach Klint Kubiak announced Kirk Cousins would be the starting quarterback in training camp.

Pictures show the Brady clan enjoying a trip with a pack of sled dogs in glorious surroundings

They seemed to spend plenty of time outdoors and enjoyed a successful fishing trip

That means Brady's No. 1 NFL Draft pick, Indiana Hoosiers national champion Fernando Mendoza, is already down the depth chart.

Brady shares Vivian and Benjamin with ex-wife Gisele. He shares Jack with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan.

Despite their separations, Brady appears to maintain a good relationship with his exes, wishing them both a happy Mother's Day earlier this year.

Brady and Bundchen split in 2022 and the Brazilian supermodel has gone on to have another child with current partner Joaquim Valente.

Moynahan and Brady were never married but instead learned they were having a baby after splitting up in late 2006.

Sports.title: LIV Golf's demise accelerates as $40m season finale is 'set to be CANCELED'... but players are still in the dark about future
Sports.content:
LIV Golf is set to cancel its season-ending team championship tournament in what may be the death knell for the Saudi-backed rebel tour.

The event, LIV Golf Michigan, was set to be held in suburban Detroit at The Cardinal at Saint John's Resort from August 27-30 and had a prize pool of $40million.

But sources tell FrontOfficeSports that an announcement will be made on Wednesday officially confirming the cancellation of the 2026 showpiece.

The cancellation comes as the future of the rebel tour that pried names like Jon Rahm, Cameron Smith, and Bryson DeChambeau from the PGA Tour remains in question after the Saudi PIF announced it would stop funding LIV after this season's end.

In the months since that announcement, players have been left somewhat in the dark over the viability for the future of the circuit.

Rumors surrounding the cancellation of the LIV regular-season finale - LIV Golf Indianapolis - also continue to be bandied about. However, that event is still scheduled to take place from August 20-23.

LIV Golf is set to cancel its team championship event with its $40m prize pool

The rebel tour, which poached Cam Smith (L) and Bryson DeChambeau (R), is seemingly on its last legs after the Saudi PIF announced plans to pull its funding at the conclusion of the season

The tour now needs to raise $350million to operate a season in 2027 after the PIF's exit

But the Michigan event seems destined for the chopping block. One source told FOS last month, 'I don't think they'll ever get to Michigan.'

Around the same time, LIV CEO Scott O'Neil couldn't guarantee that all four remaining events would go on as scheduled. One of those four events, LIV Golf UK, did get played.

Hints were dropped last week by Martin Kaymer, the captain of LIV's Cleeks GC team, who told Today's Golfer the Michigan team championship was 'highly unlikely' to be played after O'Neil held a captains meeting that left 'lingering questions' to be answered.

The final three events were scheduled to take place in the United States. In addition to the Indianapolis event, LIV Golf New York is still scheduled to go on at Trump National Golf Club in Bedminster, New Jersey.

Of the $40million prize pool, the winning squad was supposed to take home $11.2million. Both those figures are down from last year's numbers of $50m and $14m, respectively.

This is the second event to be cancelled this season, joining LIV Golf Louisiana's cancellation from back in April.

LIV is still looking for new investors to replace the funding from the PIF. The tour is hoping to raise up to $350million to keep the league running in 2027.

Sports.title: Man City's forgotten man Kalvin Phillips is set for ANOTHER loan move after being left out of Man City squad for Asia tour - with injured Jack Grealish also absent
Sports.content:
Kalvin Phillips is finalising a new loan move to Sheffield United after being left off Manchester City's squad list to tour Asia.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last month, Chris Wilder is keen to re-sign the 30-year-old, who has two years left on his contract, despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Phillips has endured a torrid time since joining City for £42 million from Leeds United and is keen to kickstart his career.

The 30-year-old former England international was desperate to make an impact, but his lack of games in recent seasons and subsequent shortage of match sharpness put him at a physical disadvantage.

The 31-cap international previously had loan spells with West Ham and Ipswich in the Premier League before linking up with Sheffield United in January.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday

Including his loan moves, he has made a total of 46 league appearances since joining City almost four years ago.

Talking to BBC Radio Sheffield towards the end of the season, Wilder said: 'He'll have a lot of people still after him. We've brought a really good pro in. He was unlucky with his injury and he's not played as much as he wanted to play.

MAN CITY TOUR SQUAD

Goalkeepers Gianluigi Donnarumma, Marcus Bettinelli, Max Chabot, Jack Wint. Defenders Rayan Ait-Nouri, Max Alleyne, Kaden Braithwaite, Josko Gvardiol, Matty Henderson-Hall, Abdukodir Khusanov, Rico Lewis, Stephen Mfuni, Vitor Reis. Midfielders Claudio Echeverri, Phil Foden, Jaden Heskey, Mateo Kovacic, Jeremy Monga, Divine Mukasa, Nico Gonzalez, Xavier Parker, Tijjani Reijnders, Floyd Samba, Antoine Semenyo, Savinho. Forwards Mahamadou Sangare, Divin Mubama, Ryan McAidoo.

'I spoke to him and said we'd love to be an option for you, your agent and your parent club if that is a possibility.

'He certainly ticks the box in terms of personality and characteristics, off the pitch and on it. If there's an opportunity I'm sure we'll try and explore that one.'

Jack Grealish has also been left out of City's pre-season tour as he continues his rehabilitation and individual training programme.

Grealish joined Everton on loan at the beginning of last season and his time with the Toffees got off to the perfect start as he notched two goals and six assists during the early months of the season.

But in January the attacker suffered a stress fracture during a game against his former club Aston Villa, which required surgery.

The injury marked the end of Grealish's season – and thereby killed his World Cup hopes - and he stayed at the Hill Dickinson club until the end of the season to undergo his rehabilitation.

He has since returned to City, posting a picture of himself on the grass last week with the caption: 'Nice to see everyone, am nearly there! Hopefully not long now till back training for good'.

There has been interest from Saudi Arabia - and Everton are also aware of his situation - but a decision on his future looks likely to come later in the window.

Savinho also wants to push through his move to Tottenham but City maintain his valuation has not been met and would want a replacement before they allow the 22-year-old to leave.

Sources at Tottenham indicate City's valuation has changed since initial talks.

City have considered the likes of Ibrahim Mbaye from PSG and Chelsea's Pedro Neto as potential wing additions.

Sports.title: Silver lining for England's 'sexy and aggressive' track Goddess: Amy Hunt misses out on Commonwealth Games gold in women's 100m final
Sports.content:
Silver lining for England's 'sexy and aggressive' track Goddess: Amy Hunt misses out on Commonwealth Games gold in women's 100m final

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

As Amy Hunt paraded through the interview room, a beaming smile and the English flag draped over her drenched shoulders, she wiggled her fingers to flash her silver rings.

‘I need to start wearing gold jewellery,’ she laughed, having just finished second in the 100 metres final. There was no shame whatsoever in her silver medal, but Hunt has always been one of life’s over achievers.

‘If anyone wants to buy some gold rings for me, that would be amazing!’ added the Cambridge University graduate.

She lost three of her acrylic nails on the starting blocks. The conditions in Glasgow were filthy, splashing and dashing through torrential rain to finish in a time of 10.98 seconds.

‘It was pretty gross on the start line,’ she said. ‘My fingers were underwater but you just have to roll with the punches at champs.’

Throughout the evening, stadium staff pushed giant squeegee machines over the surface to soak up the water. They absorb 60 litres per minute but nothing could prevent the track from turning into a 100m slip and slide.

Amy Hunt sprinted to silver in the women's 100m final at the Commonwealth Games

New Zealand's Zoe Hobbs made a fast start to the final and held off Hunt to claim the gold

Hunt, seen congratulating Hobbs, has view this all as part of her long-term project building towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games

Billy Connolly was born 15 minutes away this stadium, which is usually occupied by the Glasgow Warriors rugby team. As the city’s windswept comedian once said: ‘There are two seasons in Scotland: June and winter.’

Outside of Scotstoun, volunteers were determined not to be brought down by the washout. ‘No Scotland, no party,’ they chanted. In the uncovered stand behind the finish line, most of the party had left for shelter by the time Hunt crossed the line.

For Hunt, you suspect this is all part of a long-term project to put her in medal contention for the 200m at the 2028 Olympics. The 24-year-old has been working hard to improve her start - and it was her top-end speed pulled her back into the medal positions. So far in 2026, Hunt has set personal bests over 50, 60 and 100 metres. It will all help improve her chances the warmer climates of Los Angeles.

Here, however, it Zoe Hobbs of New Zealand won gold, surprising the field from Lane 7.

‘I had a really terrible first 60 metres,’ said Hunt. ‘So I think it just shows the calibre of my top end speed that I could dig myself out of the horrendous ditch that I dug in the first half of the race.

‘It was the first 10 for me. I'm a legitimate starter. I can get it right, and today I got it really badly wrong. My top end speed is so formidable that I was able to claw back that silver but I think gold was definitely there for the taking. I beat Zoe in the semis - and she's an incredible athlete. She ran a PB to win, but I think gold was definitely there.’

Heather Oakes was the last woman to win 100m gold for England in the Commonwealths. That was back in 1986, when 32 nations boycotted the competition because Margaret Thatcher refused to impose sanctions on South Africa's apartheid government. The wait goes on.

Many of the world’s fastest women stayed away from Glasgow this week. Olympic champion Julien Alfred, of St Lucia, was among the absentees, along with the British Virgin Islands’ Adaejah Hodge, who has clocked the fastest time in the world this year. You suspect they were not full of regret when they turned on their TV sets to see athletes huddled under umbrellas. The high jump was delayed for almost two hours.

Englishman Elliot Jones raced earlier in the evening, losing out in his 100m semi-final. The 28-year-old needed to wring out his running spikes as he headed back into the changing room. ‘There was water all over the lane,’ said Jones, who watched Cameroonian Emmanuel Eseme win the final with a Games record time of 9.83s.

‘It felt like I couldn't get any traction. I didn't feel like I was moving anywhere. It's frustrating, but everyone's got the same conditions. I got in the blocks and I was pushing water out my lanes. In between the false start and the start, the water had repoured. It's a Scottish summer, isn't it?’

This was a summer headline that Hunt was not prepared to miss out on. Her parents travelled up from Newark to watch, booking an Airbnb with her coach. Only the Commonwealths? Tell that to her mentor, the double gold medallist Darren Campbell.

‘I think it's really, really important as a track athlete,’ said Hunt, who won 200m silver in the World Championships in Tokyo last September. ‘We don't get much representation in terms of media. We're not NBA players. We're not on TV three times a week, when everyone's seeing our faces.

‘It's really, really important in terms of my journey as an athlete, my legacy is an athlete. I don't want to go on my Wikipedia page in 30 years' time and just see one or two medals. I want to see lists and lists of medals. This is my first Commonwealth Games, so it was really good to come here.’

And the Glaswegian storm clouds, at least, had a silver lining.

Sports.title: Tottenham dream 2026/27 squad as Micky van de Ven signs new deal and star striker arrives
Sports.content:
Tottenham dream 2026/27 squad as Micky van de Ven signs new deal and star striker arrives

Tottenham have already spent more than £200million in the transfer window but Roberto De Zerbi has insisted the club are not done reshaping their squad

View 3 Images Roberto De Zerbi has already had a busy summer at Tottenham Hotspur (Image: Mark Leech/Offside, Offside via Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur have already made a significant impact in the transfer market but Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed he is not finished overhauling his squad. Spurs have invested over £200million this summer, despite half of their acquisitions coming as free agents.

‌



The club's new £185m midfield partnership of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes made headlines, as did their £52m acquisition of Jan Paul van Hecke, which subsequently saw Luka Vuskovic replace the defender at Brighton. However, Tottenham have also secured shrewd deals for Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and seasoned goalkeeper Martin Dubravka.

‌



"It is not finished yet, our transfer market," De Zerbi said. " I think we can be happier at the end of this transfer market, because I spoke a lot to the owner, the board, and they want to build a very strong team for this season, but to make the base for the future to become great again.

‌



"The target now is to complete the attacking positions. We want the first target, the first level, because anyway we are already important players, but I think to start the new project we need another couple of important players, for sure."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

With De Zerbi determined to transform his forward line, it seems Spurs are poised to continue their recruitment. Here is a look at how Tottenham's squad could look at the end of the transfer window.

‌



Wantaway Tottenham star emerges on Arsenal and Chelsea radar in transfer twist READ MORE :

Jermain Defoe threatens legal action over 'untrue' Woking claims since leaving job READ MORE :

Two forwards arrive

Meeting De Zerbi's requirements, Manchester City winger Savinho could seal his switch to Spurs, having been linked with the club since last summer. The club have been pursuing a deal for the 22-year-old, although no offer has been submitted.

Savinho has shown glimpses of ability during his spell at City but Spurs will hope more regular game time can help the forward reach his potential. His acquisition would strengthen De Zerbi's choices on the left side, while Mohammed Kudus and a returning Dejan Kulusevski can compete for a place in the starting XI on the other flank.

Up front, Dominic Solanke can expect to retain his starting berth, while Mathys Tel has the manager's confidence, though one of the Premier League's most exciting prospects could bolster Tottenham's attack. Spurs are among several clubs, including fierce rivals Arsenal, linked with Bournemouth talent Eli Junior Kroupi, who netted 13 league goals last campaign.

‌



View 3 Images Savinho has been linked with Spurs (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Bournemouth have no desire to part with the 20-year-old. However, Spurs have already completed more than one surprise signing this summer and may seek to challenge the club's determination with a substantial bid.

Micky van de Ven signs new deal

Tottenham are working on a new contract for Micky van de Ven and the defender pledging his long-term future to the club would settle a crucial position in De Zerbi's side. The earlier uncertainty surrounding his and Cristian Romero's situations, coupled with the arrivals of Van Hecke and Senesi, and the return of loanee Vuskovic, left Spurs' defence in doubt.

‌



A slightly new-look defence would see Van de Ven partnering fellow Dutchman Van Hecke, as club captain Romero completes a switch to Inter Milan. Full-backs Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie will also provide continuity but fresh arrivals Senesi and Robertson will be determined to break into the manager's thinking.

View 3 Images Micky van de Ven is currently under contract until 2029 (Image: BSR Agency/Getty Images)

Between the posts, Antonin Kinsky earned a new contract following his impressive finish to the campaign and will begin the new season as first choice. Meanwhile, Juventus hold interest in Guglielmo Vicario and Dubravka's arrival indicates a reshuffle in the goalkeeping ranks.

‌



Midfield battle

Fernandes and Tonali will be tasked with anchoring Spurs' midfield next season. Yet both will recognise the need to maintain peak form as they encounter stiff competition for their positions.

Rodrigo Bentancur, Archie Gray, Conor Gallagher and Pape Matar Sarr could potentially see diminished roles next term should De Zerbi persist with deploying a number 10. Lucas Bergvall has already expressed his wish to leave the club, sparking links with various sides, and his exit could help finance De Zerbi's transfer plans.

Meanwhile, the Spurs manager will be hoping to capitalise on James Maddison's return to full fitness after he missed most of last season due to injury. The 29-year-old will also face elite competition once Xavi Simons recovers from his time out injured.

Sports.title: Arsenal signed 141-goal striker, world class £42.5m star and wonderkid from Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal signed 141-goal striker, world class £42.5m star and wonderkid from Real Madrid

Arsenal have continued to be linked with Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr

View 4 Images Arsenal have done business with Real Madrid before (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal and Real Madrid have a history of conducting business together in the transfer market. And that could be extended if the Gunners make an official approach for Vinicius Jr. The Brazilian has been linked with a move to north London after entering the final year of his contract in Spain.

‌



Mikel Arteta has become 'smitten' with the idea of signing Vini and is viewed internally as the club's priority target. Negotiations are yet to begin and the Brazil international is said to be keen on the idea of remaining in La Liga.

‌



However, he "wants to feel loved" and Arteta could provide that player-manager bond that the 26-year-old desires. If he does end up switching from one capital to another, it wouldn't represent the first time such a move has taken place.

‌



Here, Mirror Football analyses three players who previously made the switch from Spain to north London.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal can offer Vinicius Jr key non-negotiable that Real Madrid cannot after transfer update READ MORE :

The 4 transfers Arsenal must complete for Mikel Arteta to win another Premier League title READ MORE :

141-goal striker

Julio Baptista, nicknamed 'The Beast' for his physical presence, joined Arsenal on loan during the 2006/07 season from Real. Arsene Wenger had previously tried to convince the attack to head to north London but he opted for Spain instead.

‌



Jose Antonio Reyes went to Real while Baptista headed to Arsenal but he struggled to adapt to the English game. He scored just three Premier League goals across 24 appearances but found some form in cup competitions, notably scoring four against Liverpool at Anfield in a League Cup quarter-final.

View 4 Images Julio Baptista didn't exactly thrive at Arsenal (Image: Christian Liewig / Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Throughout his career, which included stints at Sevilla, Roma, Sao Paulo and CFR Cluj, Baptista scored 141 goals and assisted 34 times.

‌



£42.5m star

In 2013, Arsenal broke their club transfer record by securing Mesut Ozil for £42.5m. The attacking midfielder spent three years at Real, scoring 27 goals and assisting 80 times across 159 appearances.

He became the most expensive German player of all time with his transfer to Arsenal. Florian Wirtz now holds that title with his £116m move to Liverpool.

View 4 Images Mesut Ozil was a gamechanger for the Gunners (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

‌



Ozil's time at the Gunners was just as prolific as his playmaking in Spain, making 121 goal contributions and winning four FA Cups. The Germany international also won the World Cup one year after signing for Arsenal and earned 97 caps for his country.

However, the midfielder's time in north London ended on a sour note as he was left out of matchday squads and eventually departed the club in 2021. He had stints at Fenerbahce and Istanbul Basaksehir before retiring in 2023.

Real wonderkid

Martin Odegaard became Real's next wonderkid with his transfer from Stromsgodset in 2015. The midfielder only made 11 official appearances for the La Liga giants but was a teenager during the majority of his career in Spain.

‌



View 4 Images Martin Odegaard joined the Gunners from Real and the rest is history (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Odegaard got his first minutes for Real after coming on for Cristiano Ronaldo at the age of 16 years and 157 days old - and he still remains the club's youngest ever debutant to this day. After loans to Vitesse and Real Sociedad, the midfielder joined Arsenal temporarily to play the second half of the 2020/21 season.

He then made this move permanent, signing for the Gunners in a deal worth an initial £30m. Just a year later, Odegaard was made club captain and has gone from strength to strength since.

Article continues below

Across 234 appearances, the 27-year-old has made 88 goal contributions and recently helped win Arsenal's first Premier League title since 2004. He is contracted to the Gunners until 2028.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Mo Salah talks stall as Reds learn transfer timeline for replacement
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Mo Salah talks stall as Reds learn transfer timeline for replacement

There have been big developments surrounding former Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah's next club

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah is still without a club (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's desire to secure a new winger this summer seems to have led them to PSG's Bradley Barcola. The French forward has risen to the top of the Reds' shortlist, with PSG determined to land a big fee for the French international.

‌



Finding a successor to Mohamed Salah, who left the club this summer after nine years of goals and major trophies, was never going to be easy.

‌



Despite reportedly giving his word to Reds' head coach Andoni Iraola that he will join the club this summer, finally capturing Barcola may take an extraordinary effort from Liverpool. Last summer, the club broke their transfer record consecutively for Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak, respectively, after drawn-out negotiations.

‌



With PSG looking for £145million, the Reds could be forced to dig deep once again. Today's latest sees a transfer timeline for Barcola surface, while Salah's search for a new club appears to have stalled.

Mo Salah talks break down

Mohamed Salah looks unlikely to join Besiktas after transfer talks broke down. The sporting director of the Turkish club, Onder Ozen, told local media in candid detail that his club have walked away from negotiations with the winger.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool's Milos Kerkez explains why he chose to keep distance from Andy Robertson READ MORE :

He claimed Salah's representatives are also in conversation with another club. He said: "We contacted Salah, this also involved a financing model. Salah is a global star, a respected athlete. We met with Salah three times before the financial part of the negotiations was discussed.

"Up to this point, everything was smooth. When the financial side began, the initial smoothness slowed down from July 21st onwards. Requests began to arrive that would both disrupt the flow of information and create a deadlock in the financial process.

"I can assume that a respected athlete like Salah was unaware of this. The club has a policy, and it cannot deviate from that policy, our President has very clearly identified his position and has stayed there.

‌



View 3 Images Mohamed Salah left Liverpool at the end of last season (Image: Getty Images)

"I don't have a chance to say yes or no, Besiktas's offer, made under its own terms, is clear. If a response comes to this offer, it can be evaluated. But Besiktas will not make another offer.

"They said they are also in talks with another club, maybe they will get a result from there. The last offer we made to Salah is the final point that does not harm Besiktas' club identity."

‌



Salah is now a free agent after leaving Liverpool this summer, where he scored 257 goals and provided 123 assists in 442 appearances across all competitions.

Bradley Barcola timeline emerges

French outlet L'Equipe has stated that PSG star Barcola has given a 'verbal agreement' to sign for Liverpool. A previous report by the French publication claimed the Reds are aware they may need to exercise patience and wait for a deal for Barcola to be completed, however.

Liverpool and PSG are in talks over a possible deal for the player, but there remains a significant valuation gap between the two sides. It's believed the two clubs are happy to wait before settling on a potential fee, meaning the transfer saga could drag on all summer long, despite Barcola's verbal agreement.

‌



Various outlets have indicated that PSG value Barcola at £145m, citing Morgan Rogers' move to Chelsea for £117m from Aston Villa as one reason for this. The update follows reports that emerged over the weekend claiming that Barcola had decided against signing a new contract with PSG.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola's price tag has been set by PSG (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

His refusal to sign a new deal in Paris could leave the winger in a state of limbo, too. PSG boss Luis Enrique is said to want only those committed to the club at his disposal next season, as per The Athletic.

Article continues below

Indications are that Barcola may struggle for minutes if he remains at PSG this season and refuses to extend his contract.

Sports.content:

Sports.title: Police seize fake World Cup shirts worth £18.5m in major crackdown
Sports.content:
Police seize fake World Cup shirts worth £18.5m in major crackdown

Officers have seized more them 220,000 fake shirts, with a genuine retail value at an estimated £18.5 million, since January 2026 in a nationwide enforcement operation

View 3 Images Officers have removed more than 220,000 fake shirts from sale since January 2026 (Image: City of London Police/PA Wire)

Counterfeit football shirts and kits worth more than £18 million have been seized over the course of the World Cup, the City of London Police have said.

‌



Officers have removed more them 220,000 fake shirts from sale since January 2026 in a nationwide enforcement operation led by the force’s Police Intellectual Property Crime Unit (Pipcu). The total genuine retail value was estimated at £18.5 million, the force said.

‌



Four people were also arrested on suspicion of selling counterfeit shirts, and a further two arrests were made by other police forces. The City of London Police said their operation focused on online marketplaces and live shopping apps as well as traditional market stalls as offenders increasingly use tech platforms to sell counterfeit goods.

‌



View 3 Images Harry Kane looks dejected after the FIFA World Cup 2026 Semi Final match between England and Argentina (Image: Julian Finney - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Woman found dead at remote cottage in Renfrewshire was murdered, police say READ MORE :

Counterfeit shirts are produced in unsafe and unregulated conditions and can contain harmful materials that fail safety standards, while profits from the sales are used to fund criminal operations, police warned.

Detective Chief Inspector Amanda Lowe, head of Pipcu, said: “Counterfeit football shirts aren’t a harmless bargain, they are a key revenue stream for organised crime groups, helping to mask and fund the criminality happening behind the scenes.

‌



“As World Cup fever began to build, partners across the country came together to tackle this ever-growing issue. Our aim was simple; to ensure fans enjoyed the tournament and supporting their team in a shirt that’s safe and legitimate. “An issue of this scale demands a coordinated response, and we’ll continue working with our law enforcement, Government and industry partners to crack down on this illegal trade and the criminals who drive it.” City of London Police have also warned the sale of counterfeit goods deprives rights holders and legitimate businesses of revenue, while putting buyers’ personal data at risk and exposing them to financial fraud. “This is anything but a victimless crime,” Helen Barnham, head of enforcement engagement at the Intellectual Property Office, said. “The trade in counterfeit goods is estimated to cost thousands of jobs in the UK each year and supports other forms of serious crime – harming legitimate businesses, society and the wider economy.”

A spokesperson from the Football Association further warned fans: “We would strongly advise all fans to avoid counterfeit products. Not only are such products often poor quality but brand abuse and counterfeiting negatively impacts the FA’s role as a not-for-profit organisation that directly funds all levels of our national game.”

View 3 Images Football fans have been warned about the fake shifts (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Things to look out for

Buyers trying to assess whether a football shirt is fake have been advised to check the price, as what looks like a bargain may turn out to be a scam. If possible, they should also inspect the shirt’s quality by looking out for poor stitching – especially around the neckline and badge – low-quality fabric and a bad fit.

They should also ensure logos and tags match the manufacturer, and check that the swing tag includes a unique product code sticker and product-specific wording.

Handwritten numbers on care labels are also a sign the shirt may be a counterfeit product.

‌



Fans can also purchase from official retailers or the club’s store, verify website security, and be cautious of sites using official product photos without clear retailer credentials.

This follows reports that football fans face paying up to £90 for replica shirts after eight Premier League clubs increased their prices – raising concerns fans may be left priced out of buying their favourite kit.

Tottenham fans must now pay £90 for a replica adult first-team shirt, up £5 on last year, while a shirt for a child as young as three years old now costs £70, according to the club’s website. A shirt for just-promoted Coventry City is up £10 to £70 and the club’s children’s shirts are also up, by 25% to £60, while a baby kit costs £55.

Article continues below

Chelsea has also increased the price of its shirts by £5 to £89.99, while Ipswich Town shirts are up £6 to £65. Leeds, Bournemouth and Hull shirts are all £5 more expensive than last year.

Consumer expert Scott Dixon, from The Complaints Resolver, said on Monday: “These price rises will leave many loyal fans wondering when enough is enough. We see this year in, year out, and it smacks of blatant greed and an own goal that could backfire on clubs. These kits are overpriced by anyone’s standards and will leave many fans priced out.”

Sports.content:
Liverpool star confirms Mo Salah contact as true impact of star's exit made clear

Mo Salah remains without a club following his exit from Liverpool a year before the end of his deal but his impact at Anfield remains felt according to one of his former teammates

View 2 Images Mo Salah left Liverpool in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool star Milos Kerkez has revealed that he regularly speaks to club icon Mo Salah - but not about his next club. The Egyptian forward left Anfield in the summer on a free transfer a year before the end of his contract.

‌



It brought to an end a glittering spell on Merseyside, making 442 appearances and scoring 257 goals, with Liverpool winning two Premier League titles, the Champions League and a whole host of other trophies in that time.

‌



Despite Salah having now left the club, Kerkez has confirmed that the pair are still in close contact, but the forward has yet to confirm where he will be playing his football next.

‌



He said: “I still speak with Mo often, but I don’t know who he is signing for! We just talk about vacations.

“I looked up at the TV before we left the AXA for this tour and it showed how many goals and assists combined Mo had for Liverpool. It was 300 and something. I just walked out! What is this?! Time flies.”

‌



Kerkez added: “Now it’s a new generation with new players and hopefully, everything will be good. Dom signing his contract is very important for us. He is getting even better in that role of a leader. Everyone is really happy that he is continuing here for longer.”

When it comes to Salah, he has been linked with a number of clubs including Sporting Kansas City and Besiktas. But a move to Turkey now appears to be unlikely if sporting director Onder Ozent’s comments are anything to go by.

“We contacted Salah, this also involved a financing model. Salah is a global star, a respected athlete. We met with Salah three times before the financial part of the negotiations was discussed.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
